x: We have previously explained the interpretation of God Almighty’s statement, Ta-Sin-Mim, and we mentioned the differences among the interpreters regarding its interpretation.
As for his saying,
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
, he means that these are the verses of the Book that I revealed to you, O Muhammad, which clearly state that it is from God, and that you did not fabricate it or make it up.
Qatada, as was reported from him, said about this:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “Ta, Seen, Meem.
h
These are the verses of the clear Book
,” meaning clear, and God is its blessing, guidance, and direction.

x: And His saying,
h
We recite to you
, means:
h
We recite to you
and we narrate in this Qur’an the story of Moses and Pharaoh in truth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa’id told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
We recite to you

, [O Muhammad], from the report of Moses and Pharaoh in truth for a people who believe, means in this Qur’an their report. And His statement, for a people who believe, means for a people who believe in this Book, so that they may know that what
h
We recite to you

of their report is their report, and their souls may be reassured. Indeed, Our way with those of the polytheists who oppose you and are hostile to you is Our way with those of the Children of Israel who were hostile to Moses and those of Pharaoh and his people who believed in him: We destroy them as We destroyed them, and save them from them as We saved them.

x: God Almighty says: Pharaoh was arrogant and haughty in the land of Egypt, and he oppressed and subjugated its people until they acknowledged their servitude to him.

c: Muhammad bin Harun told us, he said: Amr bin Hammad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Indeed, Pharaoh was arrogant on earth, meaning: he was tyrannical on earth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land: meaning, he transgressed in the land. His saying,
h
And He made its people into sects
, means by sects: groups. He says: And He made its people into scattered groups.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And He made its people into sects

, meaning groups, some of whom He slaughters, some of whom He spares, some of whom He tortures, and some of whom He enslaves. God Almighty said, “He slaughters their sons and spares their women. Indeed,
h
he was among the corrupters

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: It was the affair of Pharaoh that he saw a vision in his sleep, in which a fire came from Jerusalem until it encompassed the houses of Egypt, so it burned the Copts and left the Children of Israel, and it burned the houses of Egypt. So he called the magicians, the priests, the soothsayers, and the fortune-tellers, and asked them about his vision, and they said to him: There will emerge from this country from which the Children of Israel came meaning Jerusalem, a man whose face will be the destruction of Egypt. So he ordered the Children of Israel that no boy should be born to them without them slaughtering him, and no girl should be born to them without her being left alone. And he said to the Copts: Look at your slaves who work outside, and bring them in, and make the Children of Israel do those filthy jobs. So he made the Children of Israel do the jobs of their servants, and they brought their servants in, and that is when he says: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and made its people sects meaning the Children of Israel when he made them do filthy jobs.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And He made its people into sects
, he said: He divided them between them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And He made its people into sects
, he said: groups.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And He made its people into sects
, he said: Sects are groups. His saying,
h
He weakens a group of them
, indicates that his weakening of them was his enslavement.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He enslaves a group of them, slaughters a group, kills a group, and takes a group as captives. His saying,
h
He was among the corrupters

, means that he was among those who spread corruption on earth by killing those who did not deserve to be killed, enslaving those who had no right to be enslaved, acting tyrannically on earth toward its people, and being too proud to worship his Lord.

x: His statement, And We desire is in apposition to his statement, He oppresses a group of them. The meaning of the statement is: Pharaoh exalted himself in the land and divided its people from the Children of Israel into groups, he oppressed a group of them. And We desire to bestow a favor upon those whom Pharaoh oppressed from the Children of Israel and make them leaders. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land. He said: The Children of Israel. His saying,
h
And We will make them leaders
, means rulers of the Mamluks. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We will make them leaders
, meaning the rulers. And His saying,
h
And We will make them the inheritors
, means:
h
And We will make them the inheritors
of the people of Pharaoh, who will inherit the land from the land of their destruction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We will make them the inheritors
: meaning they will inherit the earth after Pharaoh and his people.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And We will make them the inheritors
, meaning: They will inherit the earth after Pharaoh.

x: And His statement,
h
And We establish them in the land

, means: And We establish for them the land of Ash-Sham and Egypt. And We show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers, they had been informed that their destruction would be at the hands of a man from the Children of Israel, so they were afraid of that, and for that reason Pharaoh would slaughter their sons and keep their women alive. So God showed Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from the Children of Israel, at the hands of His prophet Moses, son of Imran, what they had been wary of from them, of their destruction and the destruction of their homes and dwellings.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We will establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared, something that the people feared. He said: It was mentioned to us that Haziyya visited the enemy of God, Pharaoh, and said: This year a boy will be born from the Children of Israel who will steal your kingdom, so you will pursue their children that year, killing their sons and keeping their women alive, out of fear of what Haziyya had said to him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: Pharaoh had a man who used to look after him and inform him, meaning that he was a soothsayer. So he said to him: A boy will be born this year who will take away your kingdom. So Pharaoh used to slaughter their sons and keep their women alive out of fear. That is what His saying says: And We showed Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement,
h
And We will see Pharaoh and Haman
. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as
h
And We will see Pharaoh and Haman
, meaning: And We will see, with the letter nun, in apposition to his statement,
h
And We will give them power

. The majority of the Kufian reciters recited it as And Pharaoh will see, with the letter ya from he sees, and they raised Pharaoh, Haman, and the soldiers. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings known among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning. Each of them was read by scholars among the reciters, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct, because it is known that Pharaoh would not have seen from Moses what he saw except that God Almighty showed him from him, and God Almighty would not have shown him that from him unless he saw it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement, And We will see Pharaoh and Haman.

The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra and some of the Kufians recited it as And We will see Pharaoh and Haman, meaning: And We will see, with the letter nun, in apposition to his statement, And We will give them power.
The majority of the Kufian reciters recited it as And Pharaoh will see, with the letter ya from he sees, and they raised Pharaoh, Haman, and the soldiers.
The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings known among the reciters of the regions, and they are close in meaning.

Each of them was read by scholars among the reciters, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct, because it is known that Pharaoh would not have seen from Moses what he saw except that God Almighty showed him from him, and God Almighty would not have shown him that from him unless he saw it.

x: God Almighty says, And We inspired the mother of Moses when she gave birth to Moses, to nurse him. Qatada used to say, in the meaning of that, And We inspired the mother of Moses, that We cast into her heart.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And We revealed to the mother of Moses
, a revelation that came to her from God, and was cast into her heart, but it was not a prophetic revelation, to breastfeed Moses. But when you fear for him, cast him into the river
h
and do not fear
and do not grieve... the verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We revealed to the mother of Moses
, he said: He ejaculated into her.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: Pharaoh ordered that all children born to the Children of Israel be slaughtered for one year, and that they be left alone for another year. So, during the year in which they were to be slaughtered, she became pregnant with Moses. When she wanted to give birth to him, she was saddened by his condition, so God revealed to her, Suckle him, and when you fear for him, cast him into the river.

x: The interpreters differed regarding the situation in which Moses' mother was ordered to throw Moses into the river.

Some of them said: She was ordered to throw him into the river four months after his birth, and that was when he was demanding more breastfeeding than a baby demands after falling from his mother's womb.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, Breastfeed him, and when you fear for him, he said: When he reaches the age of four months and cries and desires more breastfeeding than that, then cast him at that time into the river. That is what he said, and when you fear for him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah, he said:
m: He did not say to her: When you give birth to him, throw him into the river. Rather, he said to her: Breastfeed him, and if you fear for him, throw him into the river. She was commanded to do that. He said: I put him in a garden, and she would come to him every day and breastfeed him, and come to him every night and breastfeed him, and that would suffice him.

x: Others said: Rather, she was ordered to throw him into the river after giving birth to him and after breastfeeding him.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When she gave birth to him, she breastfed him and then called a carpenter for him, so he made him a coffin, and put the key to the coffin inside, and put it in it, and then she threw it into the sea. The most correct statement about this is that God, the Exalted, commanded Moses' mother to breastfeed him, and if she feared for him from God's enemy, Pharaoh and his soldiers, to throw him into the river. It is possible that she feared for them months after she gave birth to him, and whichever way it was, she did what God revealed to her, and there is no information that can be used as proof, nor is there any innate sense in the mind to clarify which one was which. The most correct statement about this is to say as God, the Most High, said: The river into which she was commanded to throw him was the Nile.

c: As Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: Then cast him into the sea, he said: It is the sea, which is the Nile. We have already explained that with supporting evidence, and mentioned the narration of it previously in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. His saying,
h
And do not fear

, nor grieve, means: Do not fear for your son from Pharaoh and his soldiers killing him, and do not grieve over his separation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: h
And do not fear

and do not grieve. He said: Do not fear the sea for him, and do not grieve for his separation. Indeed, We will return him to you. And His statement, Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers, means: We will return your child to you for breastfeeding so that you Surat al-Qasas 28:7 And We inspired the mother of Moses, "Suckle him, but when you fear for him, cast him into the river
h
and do not fear

and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers." will breastfeed him, and send him as a messenger, except for one whom you fear will kill him, and God did that to her and to him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: We will return him to you and send him as a messenger to this tyrant, and we will make his destruction and the salvation of the Children of Israel from the calamity they are in at his hands.

x: God Almighty says: So Pharaoh's family picked him up, seized him, and took him. Its origin is from the word l-qata'ah, which is something that is found lost and taken.

i: The Arabs say: When it suddenly comes to him without him seeking or wanting it, I found him, I found him, I found him, and I met so-and-so, and from this the rajaz poet says:
x: And I came to a spring which I gathered, but I did not find anything in vain when I came to it.
Meaning: suddenly. The commentators differed on the meaning of his saying the family of Pharaoh in this place.
Some of them said: What he meant by that is: the female slaves of Pharaoh’s wife.
Who said that?

c: Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi, who said:
m: The waves brought the Ark, raising it at one time and lowering it at another, until they brought it between the trees near Pharaoh’s house. Then the maids of Asiyah, Pharaoh’s wife, went out to wash, and they found the Ark and brought it to Asiyah, thinking that there was money in it. When Asiyah saw it, pity fell upon her and she loved it. When she told Pharaoh about it, he wanted to slaughter it, but Asiyah kept talking to him until he left it to her. He said: I fear that this one is from the Children of Israel, and that this one at his hands will be our destruction. This is what God says: So Pharaoh’s family picked him up, to become for them an enemy and a grief.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant Pharaoh’s daughter.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Ma’shara, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Qays, who said:
m: Pharaoh’s daughter was leprous. She came to the Nile and saw the Ark in the Nile, being tossed by the waves. Pharaoh’s daughter took it, and when she opened the Ark, she saw a boy. When she looked at his face, she was cured of the leprosy. She brought him to her mother and said: This boy is blessed. When she looked at him, she was cured. Pharaoh said: This is one of the boys of the Children of Israel. Come, so that I may kill him. She said: A comfort to me and you. Do not kill him.

x: Others said: He meant Pharaoh's helpers.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: Pharaoh began to sit in a council of his which he used to sit on the bank of the Nile every morning. While he was sitting, the Nile passed by with the Ark, throwing it out, and his wife, Asiya bint Muzahim, was sitting beside it. She said: This is something in the sea, so bring them to me. So his helpers went out to him and brought it. He opened the Ark and in it was a baby in its cradle. God instilled His love upon it and was kind to it. His wife, Asiya, said: Do not kill him; perhaps he may be of benefit to us or we may adopt him as a son. We do not have a more correct statement on this than what God Almighty said: So Pharaoh’s family picked him up. They have established the meaning of family in what has preceded sufficiently to repeat it here. And his saying,
h
So that he might be for them an enemy and a grief
, the speaker says: So that Moses might be for the family of Pharaoh an enemy and a grief, so they picked him up. So it is said, So the family of Pharaoh picked him up
h
so that he might be for them an enemy and a grief
. It was said: When they picked him up, they did not pick him up for that reason, but rather for what was mentioned above. But, God willing, as: Ibn Humayd narrated:

c: Salamah narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
So Pharaoh’s family picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief

, he said: So that he would eventually become an enemy and a grief, because of what God had intended for him. But that was not why they took him, rather Pharaoh’s wife said, A comfort of the eye for me and for you. So God’s statement,
h
So that he would be to them an enemy and a grief

, was based on what would happen in the end of his command to them. It is like someone saying when someone rebukes someone for an action he had done while thinking he was doing good, but his action led him to feel bad and regret it: I did this to harm yourself, and so that you would harm yourself by it. The doer, when he did that, was doing it with the hope of benefiting himself, but the outcome was contrary to what he had hoped for. Similarly, His statement,
h
So Pharaoh’s family picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief

, means: So Pharaoh’s family picked him up thinking they were doing good to themselves, so that he would be a comfort of their eye, but the outcome of their picking him up from him was their destruction at his hands. His saying,
h
An enemy and grief
, means: He will have an enemy for them in their religion, and grief over the harm that befalls them from him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
So Pharaoh’s family picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief

, an enemy to them in their religion, and a grief for what would come to them. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, read it as Wa Hazana with a fat-ha on the ha’ and the zay. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as Wa Hazana with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the zay. Al-Huzn with a fat-ha on the ha’ and the zay is a verbal noun from Hazanat Haznan I mourned for sorrow, and al-Huzn with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the zay is a noun, like al-Adad the absence and al-Adad the absence and the like. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, and despite the difference in wording, they are like nothing and nothingness, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement, Indeed, Pharaoh, Haman, and their soldiers were sinners, God Almighty says: Indeed, Pharaoh, Haman, and their soldiers were sinners towards their Lord, and for that reason Moses was an enemy and a cause of grief to them.

The correct thing to say about this is that they are two readings with similar meanings, and despite the difference in wording, they are like nothing and nothingness, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says, “
h
And Pharaoh’s wife said
, ‘This is a comfort of the eye for me and for you, O Pharaoh.’ The comfort of the eye is raised by an implied pronoun, which is this or he. And His saying, ‘
h
Do not kill him
,’ is a question from Pharaoh’s wife that he not be killed. It was mentioned that when the woman said this to Pharaoh, Pharaoh said, ‘As for you, yes, but as for me, no,’ and so it was.
Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Abu Maʿshar narrated: Muhammad ibn Qays said: Pharaoh’s wife said: “A comfort of the eye for me and for you.
h
Do not kill him

; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.” Pharaoh said: A comfort of the eye for you, but not for me. Muhammad ibn Qays said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “If Pharaoh had said: ‘A comfort of the eye for me and for you,’ it would have been for both of them.”

c: Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, who said:
m: Pharaoh took him as a son, and he was called because he was Pharaoh’s son. When the boy began to move, Asiya’s slave girl showed him a young boy. While she was dancing with him and playing with him, she handed him to Pharaoh and said: Take him, a comfort of my eye and yours. Pharaoh said: He is a comfort of your eye, not mine. Abdullah ibn Abbas said: If he had said: He is a comfort of my eye, then he would have believed in him, but he refused.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Pharaoh’s wife said, A comfort to the eye for me and for you, meaning Moses. Narrated Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid:

c: Yazid told us: Al-Asbagh bin Yazid told us: Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub told us: Saeed bin Jubair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When Pharaoh’s wife brought Moses to Pharaoh, she said: A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Pharaoh said: He will be for you, but as for me, I have no need of him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One by whom they swear, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be a comfort of the eye for him as she acknowledged, God would have guided him as He guided his wife through him, but God forbade him from that.” And his saying,
h
Do not kill him
; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son. It was mentioned that Pharaoh's wife said this when she intended to kill him.

x: Some of them said: When he was brought to her on the day he plucked him from the sea.
Some of them said: The day he plucked his beard or struck him with a stick that was in his hand. It was mentioned that she said that on the day he plucked his beard.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When Pharaoh was brought to him as a boy, he took him to him. Moses took hold of his beard and plucked it. Pharaoh said: Bring me the slaughterers, he is this one. Asiya said:
h
Do not kill him
, perhaps he may be of benefit to us or we may adopt him as a son. He was only a boy who did not understand, and he only did this from his youth.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Do not kill him
; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son. He said: Her mercy was bestowed upon him when she saw him. And his saying,
h
And they do not perceive
, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: The meaning of that is:
h
And they do not perceive
that their destruction is at his hand.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And they do not perceive
. He said:
h
And they do not perceive
that their destruction is at his hands, and in his time.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: Or We take him as a son while they do not perceive. He said: That their destruction will be at his hands.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Issa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And they do not perceive
, he said: The people of Pharaoh that they have an enemy.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And they do not feel what is happening of their situation and His situation.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: Pharaoh’s wife, Asiya, said:
h
Do not kill him
; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son, while they perceive not. God says: And they perceive not, meaning what is to come to pass, what God intends for it.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of his saying,
h
and they do not perceive
, is that the Children of Israel do not perceive that we picked him up.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Maʿshar, on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais,
m: h
Do not kill him

; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son while they do not perceive. He said: He says: The Children of Israel do not know that we picked him up. The correct statement about this is the statement of those who say: The meaning of this is: Pharaoh and his people do not know what will happen to them in terms of their destruction at his hands. We said that this is the most appropriate interpretation of it because it follows his statement, “
h
And Pharaoh’s wife said

And His saying: And when he turned his face towards Madyan, God Almighty says: And when Moses turned his face towards Madyan, proceeding towards it, turning away from the city of Pharaoh, and outside his authority, “he said: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.” And what he meant by his saying towards: towards Madyan. m: It was mentioned to me that he went out saying, My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people. Then God prepared the road to Madyan, so he left Egypt without provisions, shoes, a backpack, a dirham, or a loaf of bread, fearful and watching, until he came upon a group of people who were watering the land in Madyan.

c: Abu Ammar Al-Hussein bin Harith Al-Marwazi told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Moses left Egypt for Madyan, and between it and it was a journey of eight days. He said: It was said that it was about the distance from Kufa to Basra, and he had no food except tree leaves, and he left barefoot, and he had not reached it until his shoe fell off.

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Atham narrated to us, saying: Al-A’mash narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When Moses left Egypt for Madyan, which was eight nights away, it was said: It was about the distance from Basra to Kufa, and then he mentioned something similar. And Madyan was in that time the people of Shuaib, peace be upon him.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And when he turned towards Madyan

, and Madyan is a water source on which the people of Shuaib were, he said, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.’ As for his saying, the straight path, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it, similar to what we said about it.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, The straight path he said: The road to Madyan.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: He said, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path.’ He said: Towards the right path.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Ibad ibn Rashid told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right path. He said: The straight path.

x: God Almighty says: And when Moses came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their livestock and cattle. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: He found a group of people watering his flock. He said: A large number of people watering his flock.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said:
m: Al-Hasan, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
A nation of people
, he said: People.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: It happened that a group of people were watering the people of Madyan with livestock and sheep.

c: Ali ibn Musa and Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Dawud told us: Imran al-Qattan told us: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement, And when he came to the water of Madyan, Ali ibn Musa said: It is like the water of this place of yours, meaning the newly created place. Ibn Bashar said: It is like the water of this place of yours, meaning this place of yours. And his statement:
h
And he found two women driving them back
. He says:
h
And he found two women driving them back

from the people who were by the water. By his statement driving them back, he means that they were holding back their sheep. It is said from this: So-and-so drove his sheep and cattle back, if he wanted something of that to stray and go, so he stopped it and prevented it by driving them back.

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa said: It is not permissible to say: I drove the man back in the sense of: I detained him. Rather, this is said of sheep and camels. It has been narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I am at my cistern driving people away from it with my staff. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made driving people back. Among the driving is the statement of Suwayd ibn Kara’: I spend the night at the door of rhymes as if I am fending off a swarm of wild beasts with it. And the other said: Your staff was taken away by Banu Tamim, so you do not know with which staff to defend yourself. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, you repel means: you hold back.

c: Al-Abbas told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Asbagh told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And he found two women holding back. Meaning by that that they were holding back.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Two women who keep back
, he said: Two who hold back.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And he found two women holding back their sheep. He said: They were keeping back their sheep. The commentators differed about what these two women were trying to prevent.

x: Some of them said: They were preventing their sheep from the water until the people’s livestock left it, then they watered their livestock because they were weak.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Two women who keep back
he said: They keep their sheep away from the people until they finish and the well is empty for them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And he found two women behind them, meaning behind the people, keeping their sheep away from the water, which was the water of Madyan.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: They drive people away from their sheep.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their flocks, and he found besides them two women holding back their sheep. He said: That is, holding back their sheep, keeping the people away from their sheep.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of his companions, They both repel he said:
m: They repel people from their sheep. The more correct of the two interpretations is the one that says that it means: they keep their sheep away from people until they finish watering their livestock. We said that this is more correct because of the evidence of his statement:
h
What is the matter with you

? They said, ‘We do not water until the shepherds depart.’ This is because they only complained that they would not water until the shepherds departed, when Moses asked them about their flocks. If they had been protecting their sheep from the people, there would have been no doubt that they were informing about the reason for protecting them from the people, not about the reason for delaying their watering until the shepherds departed. And His saying: He said, ‘
h
What is the matter with you
two?’ God Almighty says: Moses said to the two women,
h
What is the matter with you
and what is your affair that you are keeping your livestock away from the people? Why don’t you water them with the livestock of the people and the Arabs? She says to the man:
h
What is the matter with you
? meaning what is your affair and your condition, as the rajaz poet said: Oh wonder what is wrong with him and me The people of Tawī said something similar to what we said about this.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Abbas told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Asbagh told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: He said to them,
h
What is the matter with you
two? Why are you isolating yourself and not watering your flocks with the people?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: He felt compassion for them and was filled with fear for them, when he saw their weakness and the people’s dominance over the water, so he said to them:
h
What is the matter with you

? And His saying: They said, ‘We will not water our flocks until the shepherds depart,’ God Almighty says: The two women said to Moses: We will not water our flocks until the shepherds depart their flocks, because we are not able to water them, but we only water our flocks with what the shepherds’ flocks leave in the cistern. Shepherds is the plural of shepherd, and the shepherd’s plural is shepherds, shepherds, and shepherds. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Abbas told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Asbagh told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: When Moses said to the two women,
h
What is the matter with you
? They said, We cannot water our flocks until the shepherds depart,
h
and our father is an old man
. That is, we cannot water our flocks until the people have been watered, and then we will follow up on their waste.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, until the shepherds depart, he said: You wait to be watered from the excess water in the troughs, the troughs of the shepherds.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “They said: We will not water our flocks until the shepherds depart. Two women, we cannot compete with the men. And our father is a very old man, he is not able to do that on his own, nor water his flocks. So we wait for the people until they have finished, then we water our flocks and leave.” The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: until the shepherds depart. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, and the majority of the reciters of Iraq, except for Abu ʿAmr, recited it as the shepherds depart with a damma on the yaʿ. Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr recited it with a fatha on the yaʿ from yaṣadur al-raʿān ‘an al-hawd. As for the others, they added a damma to the yaʿ, meaning: the shepherds depart their livestock. In my opinion, they are two recitations with close meanings, and scholars from the reciters have recited each of them, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. And his saying:
h
And our father is an old man

means: he is unable, due to old age and weakness, to water his livestock. His saying: He watered for them means that he, peace be upon him, opened for them the top of a well on which there was a stone that only a group of people could lift. Then he asked for water and watered their livestock from it.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said:
m: Surat al-Qasas 28:23 And when he came to the water of Madyan, he found there a group of people watering their flocks, and he found besides them two women driving back their flocks. He said, "
h
What is the matter with you
?" They said, "We will not water our flocks until the shepherds depart,
h
and our father is an old man

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: He opened a well for them, a stone over its mouth, and he watered them from it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: in a similar manner, and he added to it: Ibn Jurayj said: A stone that only ten men could bear.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Shureih, he said:
m: He came to a stone that only ten men could lift, so he lifted it alone.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: Moses had mercy on them when they said, We will not water our flocks until the shepherds depart,
h
and our father is an old man

. So he came to the well and pulled out a rock on the well around which the people of Madyan used to gather to lift it. Then Musa watered them with a bucket, so they watered their flocks, and they quickly returned, although they used to water their flocks from the excess water of the troughs.

c: Al-Abbas told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Asbagh told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So he watered for them so he began to scoop up a lot of water into the bucket until the first shepherds were satisfied, then they returned to their father with their sheep.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them charity, so he watered their flocks, and it was not long before he had watered their sheep.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: Moses took their bucket, then advanced to the water carrier with his remaining strength, and jostled the people for the water until he pushed them away from it, then he watered for them.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of the statement: until the shepherds depart.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, and the majority of the reciters of Iraq, except for Abu ʿAmr, recited it as the shepherds depart with a damma on the yaʿ.
Abu Jaʿfar and Abu ʿAmr recited it with a fatha on the yaʿ from yaṣadur al-raʿān ‘an al-hawd.
In my opinion, they are two recitations with close meanings, and scholars from the reciters have recited each of them, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct.

x: God Almighty says: Moses watered the two women’s livestock, then he turned to the shade of a tree which he said was a tamarisk tree.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Then he turned Moses to the shade of a tamarisk tree and said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, in need.

c: Al-Abbas told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Asbagh told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Saeed Ibn Jubayr told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Moses turned to a tree and took shelter in its shade, “and said: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, in need.”

c: Al-Husayn ibn Amr al-Anqazi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Israel narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: I urged my camel on for two nights until I reached Madyan in the morning. I asked about the tree under which Moses had taken refuge. It was a lush green tree, so I urged my camel towards it, as it was hungry. My camel took it and treated it for a while, then vomited it out. So I supplicated to God for Moses, peace be upon him, and then I left. And His statement, And he said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, in need.’ It was mentioned that the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, said this statement while he was in great difficulty, and he mentioned it to the two women as an allusion to them, so that perhaps they would feed him because of his intense hunger. It was said that the good about which the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, Indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, in need, what he meant by it was a full stomach of food. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When Moses fled from Pharaoh, he was struck by a severe hunger, to the point that his intestines could be seen from the outside of his peritoneum. So when he had given the two women water to drink and taken refuge in the shade, he said, My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, in need.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Anbasa told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And when he came to the water of Madyan

, he said: He came to the water and the greenery of the plants could be seen in his stomach from his emaciation, and he said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.’ He said: Satisfaction.

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman Al-Awdi told me: Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when he came to the water of Madyan
, he said: He came to the water, and the greenness of the plants could be seen in his stomach from emaciation.

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman told me: Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Indeed, I am, for whatever good you send down to me, needy. He said: Satisfaction on that day.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement, My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, needy. He said this and he had neither a dirham nor a dinar with him. He said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, I am, for whatever good you send down to me, in need. He said: He only asked for food.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah bin Al-Fadl told us, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, needy.’ He said: He did not ask his Lord for anything but food.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need.’ He said: Ibn Abbas said: Moses said, If a person wanted to look at the greenness of his intestines from the intensity of hunger, and he does not ask God for anything but a bite to eat.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need. He said: The Prophet of God was in difficulty.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, I am, for whatever good you send down to me, needy. He said: It reached me that Moses said it and the woman heard it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
From the good of a poor person
, he said: Food.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
From the good of a poor person
, he said: Food.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, I am, for whatever good you send down to me, in need, he said: Food is sought, he did not have food with him, but he asked for food.

x: God Almighty says: Then one of the two women for whom he had watered came to Moses, walking shyly before Moses, covering her face with her garment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib and Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar bin Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab,
m: may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement,
h
Then one of them came to him walking shyly
, he said: Covered by the sleeve of her shirt, or the sleeve of her shirt.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Hammad ibn Amr al-Asadi, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Umar,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: She placed her hand on her face, covering it.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf:
m: One of them came to him walking shyly. He said: She covered her face with her hands. He said: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf, in a similar manner.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Nawf:
m: One of them came to him walking shyly. He said: She was saying with her hands on her face, and my father put his hand on his face.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr Ibn Maymun:
m: One of the two women came to him walking shyly. He said: She was not a shy woman, going out and coming in, putting her garment over her face, saying: My father is calling you to reward you for having watered our flocks.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab,
m: may God be pleased with him: One of them came to him walking shyly. He said: She was not a woman of the early age, going out and coming in, saying with her hand on her face: My father is calling you to reward you for having watered our flocks.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us: Qara ibn Khalid told us:
m: I heard al-Hasan say, regarding His statement:
h
Then one of them came to him walking shyly
, he said: Far from obscenity.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: She walked shyly. He said: She came to him walking shyly before him.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: One of them came to him walking shyly. He said: Placing her hand on her forehead. And His statement: She said, ‘Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered our flocks for us.’ God Almighty says: The woman who came to Moses walking shyly said, Indeed, my father invites you that he may reward you for having watered our flocks for us. She said, He may reward you for having watered our flocks for us. And his saying,
h
So when he came to him and told him the story

, means: Moses went with her to her father, and when he came to her father and told him his story with Pharaoh and his Coptic people, her father said to him, Do not fear, for you have escaped from the wrongdoing people, meaning: from Pharaoh and his people, because he had no authority over our land to which he had come. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Abbas told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Asbagh told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Saeed bin Jubair told us on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Abu Al-Jaritayn was surprised at the speed with which they had set out with their sheep, full and full, so he said: You two have a special matter today.

x: I think he said:

c: So they told him
m: the story, and when Moses came to him, he spoke to him, “He said: Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.” Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: When the two girls returned to their father quickly, he asked them, and they told him the report of Musa. So he sent one of them to him, and she came to him walking shyly, and he was shy of him. She said: My father invites you to reward you for having watered our flocks for us. So he stood with her and said to her: Go, so she walked in front of him, and the wind hit her, and he looked at her rump, so Musa said to her: Walk behind me, and show me the way if I make a mistake.

c: So when the old man came and told him
m: the story, he said: Do not fear. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people.
b.via: So when the old man came and

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Then one of them came to him walking shyly

. She said: ‘My father invites you that he may reward you for having watered our flocks.’” He said: Mutraf said: By God, if the Prophet of God had anything to say, he would not have followed their two tastes. Rather, what drove him to that effort was:
“So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said: ‘Do not fear. You have been saved from the wrongdoing people.’”

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: They returned to their father at a time when they usually did not return, and he was displeased with their situation. He asked them, and they told him the report. He said to one of them: Hurry up and bring it to me. She came to him shyly and said: My father invites you to reward you for having watered our flocks. So he stood with her, as Layyin mentioned, and said to her: Walk behind me and describe the road to me, and I will walk in front of you, for we do not look at the backs of women. So when he came to him, he told him the report and what he had told him about his country.

“So when he came to him and related to him the story, he said: ‘Do not fear. You have been saved from the wrongdoing people.’” She had told her father what he had said: We do not look at the backs of women.

x: God Almighty says: One of the two women for whom Moses had watered said to her father when Moses came to him, and the name of one of them was Safoor, and the name of the other was Leah, and it was said: Sharaf likewise.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Wahb ibn Sulayman al-Ramadi told me, on the authority of Shuʿayb al-Jubei, he said:
m: The names of the two slave girls were Leah and Zipporah, and the wife of Moses was Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro, the priest of Midian, and the priest was a rabbi.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: One of them was Zipporah, the daughter of Jethro, and her sister was Sharfa, also called Leah, and they were the two who used to drive away the sheep. As for their father, there is a difference of opinion about his name.

x: Some of them said that his name was Jethro.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, who said:
m: The one who hired Moses, the son of Akhbi Shu’aib, was Jethro.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, who said:
m: The one who hired Moses was Jethro, son of Akhibi Shu’aib, peace be upon him.

x: Others said: Rather, his name is: Yathra.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Al-Ala’ bin Abdul-Jabbar told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The one who hired Moses: to enrich the master of Midian.

c: Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Abdi Ismail bin Al-Haitham told me: Abu Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The one who hired Moses: He enriched the ruler of Midian.

c: Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Abdi Ismail bin Al-Haitham told me: Abu Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The woman’s father’s name was Yathra.

x: Others said, rather his name is Shuʿayb, and they said: He is the Prophet Shuʿayb, peace be upon him.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Qara ibn Khalid told us:
m: I heard al-Hasan say: They say Shuʿayb was the companion of Moses, but he was the master of the people of the water on that day.

x: “This is something that can only be known through narration, and no narration of that kind requires proof. So no statement on that matter is more correct than what God, the Most High, said: “And he found besides them two women keeping back…” One of them said, ‘
h
O my father

, hire him.’ What she meant by her statement is: Hire him to tend your livestock. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy. She said: The best one you can hire for tending your livestock is the strong one who can protect and care for your livestock, the trustworthy one whose betrayal you do not fear in what you entrust him with. It was said that when she said that to her father, he was surprised by her description of him and said to her: And how do you know that? She said: “As for his strength, I have never seen him treat others like he treats others when watering at the well. As for his trustworthiness, I have never seen him lower his gaze from me.”
In this way, the report came from the people of interpretation.
Who said that?
Ibn Wakee' narrated: Yazid narrated:

c: Al-Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: h
One of the two women said
h
O my father

, hire him, for the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.'" Jealousy kept him from saying: How do you know his strength and trustworthiness? She said: "As for his strength, I did not see him when he watered our crops. I have never seen a man stronger than him in that task. As for his trustworthiness, he looked when I came to him and stared directly at him. When he knew I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it, and he did not look at me until I delivered your message to him. Then he said: 'Walk behind me and describe the way to me.' He would not have done that unless he is trustworthy." Her father was pleased and believed her and thought what she had said about him.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement to Moses, The best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy, meaning: trustworthy in what he is entrusted with, trustworthy with what he is entrusted with.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
One of the two women said
h
O my father

, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.’” He said: When Moses had watered their flocks for them, and she saw his strength, and moved a stone in the well, thirty men could not do it, so he removed it from the well and set off with the girl when she called him, and he said to her, Walk behind me and I will be in front of you, for he did not want to see anything behind her that God had forbidden anyone to look at, and it was a windy day. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Na’im, regarding the statement of God, “
h
O my father

, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.” Her father said to her: What did you see of his trustworthiness? She said: When I called him, I walked in front of him, and the wind kept blowing my clothes, making my body slip. He said: Stay behind me, and when you reach the road, go. She said: And I saw him filling the tank with a single bucket.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The strong, the trustworthy, he said: He lowered his gaze from them. Muhammad ibn Amr said in his hadith, when, or until he watered for them and they left. And Al-Harith said in his hadith: until he watered without hesitation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He opened a well and put a stone in its mouth, and he watered for them from it. Al-Amin: He lowered his gaze from them when he watered for them, so they left.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar and Hani’ bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy. He said: He lifted a stone that no one could lift except a group of people.

c: Ibn Wakee' told us: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said:
m: Amr ibn Maymun said, regarding His statement, The Strong, the Trustworthy, that it was a windy day, so he said: Do not walk in front of me, lest the wind blow you to me, but walk behind me and show me the way. He said: So he said to her: How did you know his strength? She said: The stone could not be lifted by more than ten people, so he lifted it by himself.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Muawiyah narrated to me, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Artah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Shuraih,
m: regarding His statement, The Strong, the Trustworthy, he said: As for his strength, it reached a stone that could only be lifted by ten people, so he lifted it alone. As for his trustworthiness, it walked in front of him and the wind described it, so he said to it: Walk behind me and describe the path for me.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Zaida, on the authority of Al-A’mash, who said:
m: I asked Tamim ibn Ibrahim: How do you recognize his trustworthiness? He said: In his eyes, lowering his eyes from her.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy. He said: The strong in his craft, the trustworthy in what he is in charge of. He said: It was mentioned to us that what she saw of his strength was that he did not wait long for her livestock to drink water from them, and that the trustworthiness that she saw from him was that when she came to call him, he said to her: Stay behind me, and he did not want her to turn her back on him, so that is what she saw of his strength and trustworthiness.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
O my father

, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.” He said: We have been informed that his strength was the speed with which he watered their sheep. And we have been informed that he filled the cistern with a single bucket. As for his trustworthiness, he ordered her to walk behind him.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
One of the two women said
h
O my father

, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.’” She was the slave girl who had invited him. The old man said, “You saw this strength when he pulled out the rock. Did you see his trustworthiness? How do you know what it is?” She said, I walked in front of him, and he did not want me to betray him, so he ordered me to walk behind him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “
h
One of the two women said
h
O my father

, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy.’” He said to her, How do you know of his strength and trustworthiness? She said, “As for his strength, it is that he removed the rock that was over the well of the family of so-and-so, and he would not remove it with less than seven people. As for his trustworthiness, when I came to call upon him, he said, ‘Stay behind two people and show me your house.’ So I knew that was a sign of trustworthiness from him.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Surat al-Qasas 28:
m: h
One of the two women said
h
O my father
, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and the trustworthy." Ibn Ishaq: “One of them said, ‘
h
O my father

, hire him. The best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one.’” When she saw his strength and his saying to her what he said: Walk behind me, so that he does not see anything he dislikes from her, this increased his desire for him.

x: God the Almighty says: He said The father of the two women for whom Moses watered their flocks to Moses: I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you hire me for eight years. What he means by his saying on condition that you hire me is: on condition that you reward me for marrying her to him and shepherding my livestock for eight years, from the people's saying: May God reward you, so he will reward you, meaning: May God reward you. The Arabs say: I hired the hired woman, meaning: I gave her that, just as one says: I took it, so I will take it.

Some of the Arab scholars from Basra narrated that the Arabic language is: I hired my slave, so he is rewarded, and I hired him, so he is hired, meaning: I did it. He said: Some of them said: I hired him, so he is hired, meaning the one who did it. It seems that her father, in my opinion, made the dowry of his daughter whom Moses married him the dowry of Moses's herding his livestock for eight years, and the years are the years. And His saying, And if you complete ten, it is from you, means: If you complete the eight years as ten that I stipulated upon you by marrying you to one of my daughters, and I made it ten years, then it is a kindness from you, and it is not from what I stipulated upon you because of your marrying my daughter. And I do not want to make it difficult for you by stipulating the eight years as ten upon you. You will find me, God willing, among the righteous in fulfilling what I said to you.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: You will find me, God willing, among the righteous, meaning in good company and fulfilling what you said.

x: God Almighty says: Moses said to the father of the two women, ‘This is between you and me.’ That is, what you said, that you would marry me to one of your two daughters on the condition that I would pay you eight years of wages, is obligatory between you and me, and each of us must fulfill what he has obligated his partner to do. And his saying,
h
Whichever of the two terms you complete

, he says: Whichever of the two terms of the eight and ten Hajjs you complete, he says: I finished them and I paid you back the grazing of your sheep and cattle. There is no aggression against me, he says: You have no right to transgress against me, so you demand more from me than that. And ma in his saying,
h
Whichever of the two terms is a conjunction that connects it to
, meaning permanently.

i: The Arabists claim that this is more common in the speech of the Arabs than any, and he recited the words of the poet:
x: Whichever one I follow, I am keen on following the traces of the one I follow.
Abbas bin Mirdas said: Whatever evil there is, it will be taken to the place where it will not be seen. And his saying,
h
And God is witness to what we say
. Ibn Ishaq saw this saying from the father of the two women.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: Moses said, “That is between me and you.
h
Whichever of the two terms you fulfill

, there is no transgression against me.” He said, “Yes. And God is Witness over what we say.” So he married him and stayed with him, providing for him, and working for him in tending his sheep, as much as he needed from him. Moses’ wife was Safura or her sister: Sharaf or Liya.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: The slave girl who invited him is the one he married.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, he said to him: I want to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you serve me...to the end of the verse. He said: Which of them do you want to marry me to? He said: The one who invited you. He said: No, except that she is innocent of what you brought upon yourself. He said: She is like that with you, so he married her. And in a manner similar to what we said about His statement,
h
Whichever of the two terms you fulfill
, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: He said, ‘That is between me and you, whichever of the two terms I fulfill.’ Either eight or ten.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Lahi’ah told me, on the authority of ‘Amara ibn Ghaziya, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad,
m: and a man asked him, Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no aggression against me. He said: Al-Qasim said: I do not care which of the two it is, it is only an appointment and a judgment. And his saying,
h
And God is witness to what we say
, means: God is witness and guardian over what each one of us has obligated his companion to do with himself by this saying.

c: Like what Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And God is witness to what we say

, he said: Witness to the words of Moses and his brother-in-law. And it was mentioned that when Moses and his companion made this contract between them, he ordered one of his two daughters to give Moses a staff from the staffs that shepherds have, so she gave it to him.

x: Some of them said that it was the staff that God made for him as a sign.
Some of them said: That was a staff that Gabriel, peace be upon him, gave him.
Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The father of the two women ordered one of his two daughters to come to him, meaning to come to Moses with a staff. So she came to him with a staff, and that staff was a staff that an angel had entrusted to him in the form of a man, so he gave it to him. Then the girl entered, took the staff, and brought it to him. When the old man saw it, he said: No, bring him another one. So she threw it down, intending to take another, but nothing would fall into her hand except this one. He kept repeating it, and all the time nothing would fall into her hand except this one. When he saw that, he went to it, took it with him, and tended with it. Then the old man regretted it and Surat al-Qasas 28:28 He said, "That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there is no aggression against me. And God is Witness over what we say." said: It was a trust. So he went out to meet Moses. When he met him, he said: Give me the staff. Moses said: It is my staff, but he refused to give it to him. They argued and agreed to make the first man they met take between them. Then an angel came to them walking and said: Put it on the ground, and whoever carries it, it is his. The old man struggled with it but could not bear it, and Moses took his hand. So he raised it, and the old man left it to him, and he took care of it for ten years. Abdullah ibn Abbas said, Moses was more deserving of fulfillment.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: He said, meaning the slave girl’s father, when Moses married her to Moses: Enter that house and take the staff, so he leaned on it and entered. When he stood at the door of the house, that staff flew to him, so he took it and said: Return it and take another in its place. He said: So he returned it, then he went to take another, and it flew to him as it was, so he said: I will not return it. He did that three times, then he said: Return it, so he said: I cannot find anything else today, so he turned to his daughter and said to his daughter: Your husband is a prophet. It was mentioned that the miracle was a stick that Gabriel, peace be upon him, gave to Moses.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr, he said:
m: I asked Ikrimah, he said: As for the staff of Moses, Adam left Paradise with it, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, took it after that, and met Moses with it at night, and gave it to him.

x: God Almighty says: So when Moses fulfilled the term upon which he had parted from his companion, when he married him his daughter. He mentioned that the two terms he fulfilled, he completed and perfected them, and that was the ten years, although some scholars have narrated from him that he said: He added ten more to the poem. It was mentioned that he said: What was decided from that is the ten pilgrimages.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: I asked Ibn Abbas: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The better of the two and the more fulfilling of the two.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: who was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed them and gave them their final form.

c: Muhammad bin Amara told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of his brother, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Moses fulfilled the last of the two terms.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Ibn Abbas was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed them and fulfilled them. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated: Ibn Ishaq narrated: Hakim ibn Jubayr narrated: Saʿid ibn Jubayrin said: A Jew in Kufa said to me while I was preparing for Hajj: “I see that you are a man who seeks knowledge. Tell me which of the two terms Moses fulfilled?” I said: “I do not know. I am now going to the scholar of the Arabs,” meaning Ibn Abbas, and ask him about it. When I arrived in Mecca, I asked Ibn Abbas about it and informed him of what the Jew had said. Ibn Abbas said: “He fulfilled the greater and better of the two terms. When a prophet promises something, he does not break it.” Saʿid said: “So I arrived in Iraq and met the Jew and told him. He said: ‘He spoke the truth, and this was not revealed to Moses. And God knows best.’” He said: Yazid told us, he said:

c: Al-Asbagh bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abi Ayyub, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: A Christian man asked me: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? I said: I do not know, and at that time I did not know. So I met Ibn Abbas and mentioned to him what the Christian had asked me about. He said: Didn’t you know that eight were obligatory upon him, and the Prophet of God did not omit anything from them? And you know that God fulfilled the term He promised Moses for ten years.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And when Moses had fulfilled the term, he said: Ibn Abbas told us, he said: The Prophet of God grazed the most abundant and best of them on him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: The one that fulfilled and completed the most.”

c: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told us: al-Hamidi Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told us: Sufyan told us: Ibrahim ibn Yahya ibn Abi Yaqub told us, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I asked Gabriel: Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill? He said: He completed and perfected them.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said:
m: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, ‘Which of the two terms did Moses fulfill?’ He said, ‘I will ask Israfil.’ So he asked him, and he said, ‘I will ask God, the Blessed and Exalted.’ So he asked him, and he said, ‘The most righteous and most fulfilling of the two.’” It was mentioned that he said: He completed the ten Hajj pilgrimages and added another ten to the ten.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us

m: When the Prophet of God, Moses, called his companion to postpone the term that had been set between them, his companion said to him: Every ewe that gave birth to a color other than its own, you will have a child. And His saying,
h

, and perceived a fire from the side of the mountain, God Almighty says:
h
