and was setting out with his family, heading with them to his home in Egypt, he perceived from the side of the mountain, meaning by His saying, perceived: he saw and sensed, as Al-Ajjaj said: Anas Kharban was in a space where he spread his wings from the mountain and passed by.

x: The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this. We mentioned the narration about this before, but here we mention some of what we did not mention before.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “He saw a fire on the side of the mountain. He said
h
to his family

: Stay here, for I have seen a fire.” That is, I sensed a fire. We have explained the meaning of the mountain previously with its evidence, and what it contains of the narration from the people of interpretation. And his saying, “
h
To his family
: Stay here, for I have seen a fire.” He says: Moses said
h
to his family

: Wait and be patient, for I have seen a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from it meaning from the fire report or a burning ember. He says: Or I will bring you a thick piece of wood in which there is fire, and it is like a stump from the root of a tree. And from this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: Layla's woodcutters began to seek her abundantly, without mooing or groaning. There are three dialects for the Arabic language regarding Jadhwa: Jadhwa with a kasra on the jim, which is how the reciters of Hijaz and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it, and it is the most famous of the three dialects there. And Jadhwa with a fatha on the jim, which is also how some of the reciters of Kufa read it. Although these three dialects are well-known in the speech of the Arabs, I like reading with the most famous of them, even though I do not deny the reading of those who read with a different one. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about the meaning of the ember.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,

or a spark of fire
, meaning Shihab.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or a burning ember. The burning ember is the base of a tree in which there is fire.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,

h
or a spark of fire
, said: The palm fronds have fire in them. Muammar said, and Qatada said,
h
or a spark of fire
: or a flame from the fire.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
or a spark of fire
, he said: the root of a tree.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Or a spark of fire
, he said: The root of a tree.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement,
h
Or a spark of fire
, he said: The spark is the stick of wood in which there is fire, that is the spark. His saying,
h
Perhaps you may warm yourselves
, means: Perhaps you may warm yourself with it from the cold, and it was in winter.

evidence.text: There are three dialects for the Arabic language regarding Jadhwa: Jadhwa with a kasra on the jim, which is how the reciters of Hijaz and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read it, and it is the most famous of the three dialects there.
And Jadhwa with a fatha on the jim, which is also how some of the reciters of Kufa read it.
Although these three dialects are well-known in the speech of the Arabs, I like reading with the most famous of them, even though I do not deny the reading of those who read with a different one.

x: God Almighty says: When Moses came to the fire which he perceived from the side of the Mount, “he was called from the right bank of the valley.” By bank he means the shore, which is the side of the valley and its border. The shore is the collection of shores and shores. The shore: the shores, and the right: an adjective from the shore on the right of Moses. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, from the right bank of the valley, Ibn Amr said in his hadith, at the mountain. Al-Harith said in his hadith, from the right bank of the valley at the mountain, to the right of Moses.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And when he came to it, he was called from the right bank of the valley. He said: The valley split to the right of Moses near the mountain. His saying,
h
In the blessed spot
, is related to the beach. The interpretation of the words: When he came to it, God called to Moses from the right bank of the valley
h
in the blessed spot
of the tree: O Moses, indeed I am God, Lord of the worlds. It was said that the meaning of his saying from the tree is: at the tree.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, So when he came to it, he was called from the right side of the valley
h
in the blessed spot
from the tree. He said: He was called from near the tree, O Moses, indeed I am God, Lord of the worlds. It was said that the tree from which Moses called to his Lord was a bramble tree.

x: Some of them said that it was a blackberry tree.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
The blessed spot from the tree
, he said: The tree is bramble. Muammar said, on the authority of Qatada: Moses’ staff was made of bramble, and the tree is made of bramble.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone
m: who is not accused, on the authority of some of the people of knowledge: I saw a fire. He said: He went out towards it, and it was a bramble tree.

x: Some of the People of the Book say: It is a bramble tree.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: I saw the tree from which Moses, peace be upon him, was called, a brown, green, luxuriant tree.

x: God Almighty says: It was called to Moses, O Moses, indeed I am God, Lord of the worlds, * And throw down your staff. So Moses threw it down, and it became a serpent, scurrying about. When Moses saw it twitching he says: moving and agitated as if it were a jinn. The jinn is one of the jinn, and it is a well-known type of snakes, and some of them are large. The meaning of the statement is: as if it were a jinn among the snakes. And it turned its back he says: Moses turned its back, fleeing from it.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: He turned back fleeing from it, and did not return meaning: he did not return on his heels. We have already mentioned the narration on this matter, and what the people of interpretation have said previously, so we did not want to repeat it. However, we will mention in this regard some of what we did not mention there.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And he did not turn back. He says: And he did not turn back: meaning he did not turn back from fear.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And he did not wait. He said: He did not wait. And His saying, O Moses, come forward and do not fear, God Almighty says: So Moses intended: O Moses, come forward to me and do not fear what you are fleeing from. You are among those who are safe, from being harmed by it, it is only your staff.

x: And his saying,
h
Put your hand in your pocket
, means: put your hand in, and there are two versions of this: I put it in, and I put it in. In your pocket, means: in the pocket of your shirt.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Put your hand into your pocket: meaning into the pocket of your shirt. We have previously explained the reason why he was ordered to put his hand in his pocket rather than his sleeve. His saying,
h
It comes out white without any defect
, means: It comes out white without any leprosy.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Ibn al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Qara bin Khalid told us, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Put your hand into your bosom
; it will come out white without blemish. He said: So it came out like a lamp, and Moses was certain that he had met his Lord. His saying,
h
And fold your wing towards you
, means: And fold your hand towards you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, And draw your wing towards you, he said: your hand.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And draw your wing towards you. He said: Its wings are the arm. The upper arm is the wing. And the hand is the hand. Draw your hand to your wing; it will come out white without disease. His saying, from the terror, means: from the fear and terror that you experienced from witnessing what you witnessed of the terror of the snake. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, of fear, he said: separation.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And draw your wing towards you from fear: meaning from terror.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, from the fear, he said: from what entered him of fear from the snake and the fear, and he said: that is the fear, and he read the statement of God, they call upon Us in hope and fear, he said: fear and aspiration. The reciters differed in their recitation of this word. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read it as min ar-rahb with a fat-ha on the ra’ and the ha’. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as min ar-rahb with a damma on the ra’ and a sukoon on the ha’. The statement about this is that they are two readings with the same meaning and are well-known among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct. And His statement,
h
These are two proofs from your Lord

, meaning that God Almighty says: These two things that I showed you, O Moses, of the staff turning into a snake, and your hand, while it was brown, shining white without leprosy, are two proofs. He says: Two signs and two arguments. The root of proof is explanation. It is said to a man who says something when he is asked to provide evidence for it: Give me your proof for what you say, meaning give me an explanation and confirmation of that. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
These are two proofs from your Lord
. The staff and the hand are two signs.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
These are two proofs from your Lord
, two clarifications from your Lord.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
These are two proofs from your Lord
. These are two proofs.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
These are two proofs from your Lord

, then he recited, Bring your proof (al-Baqarah 2:111 - Al-Biya’: 24 - al-Naml 27:64 - al-Qasas 28:75), on that there is a verse that we know, and he said: Two proofs, two signs from God. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement fa-dhanak. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr, recited it fa-dhanak with a light nun because they are both nuns. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr recited it fa-dhanak with a heavy nun. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for its emphasis.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The emphasis on the nun is due to its heaviness for emphasis, just as they included the lam in that.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It was emphasized to differentiate it from the nun that is dropped for the addition, because these two and these two are not added. Another of them said: It is from the language of those who say: This said that, so they added an alif to the alif. Likewise, they added a nun to the nun to separate them from the proper nouns. He said about those two that it was only for those who said: These two, oh this, so they disliked the dual of the addition so they followed it with the lam, because the addition is followed by the lam. Abu Amr used to say: The emphasis on the nun in those two is from the language of the Quraysh. To Pharaoh and his nobles means: To Pharaoh and the nobles of his people, an argument against them, and an indication of the truth of your prophethood, O Moses. Indeed, they were a wicked people means: Indeed, Pharaoh and his nobles were a disbelieving people.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this word.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read it as min ar-rahb with a fat-ha on the ra’ and the ha’.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as min ar-rahb with a damma on the ra’ and a sukoon on the ha’.
The statement about this is that they are two readings with the same meaning and are well-known among the reciters of the regions, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct.
The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement fa-dhanak.
The majority of the reciters of the regions, except Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr, recited it fa-dhanak with a light nun because they are both nuns.
Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr recited it fa-dhanak with a heavy nun.

x: God Almighty says: Moses said: My Lord, I have killed a person from among Pharaoh’s people, and I fear that if I go to them and do not explain myself, they will kill me because I have a difficulty in speaking, and I cannot clearly articulate what I want to say. My brother Aaron is more eloquent than I. He says: He is better at explaining what he wants to explain. So send him with me as a support, meaning: a helper who will confirm me: that is, he will explain to them what I am talking to them about.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I, so send him with me as a support to confirm me: meaning, to explain to them on my behalf what I am saying to them, for he understands what they do not understand. It was said: Moses asked his Lord to support him with his brother, because when two people come together to tell a story, the soul is more at ease believing them than believing the story of one person.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Then send him with me as a support to confirm me
, because two are more likely to be confirmed than one. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Then send him with me as a support to confirm me
, he said, a helper.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, a support that will support me: meaning, a helper.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: So that he will believe me.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: A support that will confirm me, meaning: so that he will confirm me.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: h
Then send him with me as a support to confirm me
. He said: So that he would confirm me.

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: A support that will support me means: so that he will support me. In Arabic, support means: assistance. It is said from it: I supported so-and-so in his matter, meaning I sufficed him and helped him. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement yasdiqni he believes in me. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read it rad'a yasdiqni in the jussive mood of yasdiqni. Asim and Hamza read yasdiqni in the rafah. Whoever raised it made it a conjunction to the rad'a, meaning: send him with me as a support from his description who believes in me. Whoever jazm it made it an answer to his statement so send him, for if you send him he will believe in me, in the form of a statement. The nominative reading in that is the more preferable of the two readings to me, because it is a request from Moses to his Lord to send his brother to help him with this description. And his saying,
h
I fear that they will lie
, means: I fear that they will not believe me when I say to them that I was sent to you.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of his statement yasdiqni he believes in me.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Basra read it rad'a yasdiqni in the jussive mood of yasdiqni.
The nominative reading in that is the more preferable of the two readings to me, because it is a request from Moses to his Lord to send his brother to help him with this description.

x: God Almighty says: God said to Moses, We will strengthen you, meaning, We will strengthen you and support you with your brother. The Arabs say when a man honors another, supports him, and protects him from those who want to wrong him: So-and-so has strengthened so-and-so’s arm, which is from the verb ‘ādaduhu in his matter’: if he aids him. From this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: I supported her with a weak stick, as if it were an ivory cane, now hidden Meaning: A bow supported by an arrow. There are four different forms of the word 'Udhd: the best of which are: 'Udhd, then 'Udhd, then 'Udhd, and 'Udhd. All of these are pluralized as 'A'dhd. And His saying,
h
And We will give you both authority
, means: And We will give you both an argument.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
For you both is authority is an argument

c: Al-Qasim told us:
m: He said: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And We will give you both authority
. Authority means proof. And His statement,
h
So they will not reach you both
, means, So Pharaoh and his people will not reach you with harm. And His statement,
h
With Our signs
, means,
h
So they will not reach you both
, Pharaoh and his people.
h
With Our signs
, you and those who follow you will be the victors. The preposition with in His statement,
h
With Our signs is a relative clause of the victors
. The meaning of the statement is, You and those who follow you will be the victors. Pharaoh and his people,
h
With Our signs
, meaning, With Our proof and authority that We will give you both.

x: God Almighty says: So when Moses and his chiefs came to Pharaoh with Our clear proofs and arguments, that they were proofs testifying to the truth of what Moses had brought from his Lord, they said to Moses: This that you have brought us is nothing but magic that you invented before you and invented as a lie and a falsehood. And we have not heard of this that you are calling us to, of the worship of the one whom you are calling us to worship, among our ancestors and forefathers who passed away before us.

God Almighty says, And Moses said, responding to Pharaoh, My Lord knows best who among us is right and who is wrong, and who has brought guidance to the right path and clarification of the clear proof from Him, and who among us has the praiseworthy outcome in the Hereafter. This is an opposition from the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, to Pharaoh, and a beautiful way of addressing him, as he left out saying to him: Rather, the one who deceived his people, destroyed his soldiers, and led his followers astray is you, not me. Rather, he said, My Lord knows best who has brought guidance from Him and who will have the final outcome in the Hereafter. Then he went further in denouncing the enemy of God with a more beautiful way of addressing him, saying, Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
The unbelievers in God Almighty will not succeed and will not achieve their goal.
By that, Pharaoh means that he will not succeed and will not succeed because of his disbelief in Him.

God Almighty says: Pharaoh said to the nobles and leaders of his people, O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than me. So worship Him and believe what Moses brought you, that you and he have a lord other than me and a god other than me. Then light a fire for me, O Haman, upon the clay. He said, Make me a brick. He mentioned that he was the first to bake bricks and build with them.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: So kindle for me, O Haman, on the clay. He said: On the mud, it is cooked milk. Ibn Jurayj said: The first person to order the making of bricks and build with them was Pharaoh.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then light a fire for me, O Haman, upon the clay. He said: So he was the first to cook bricks to build the palace with.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding God’s statement, Then kindle for me, O Haman, upon the clay, he said: The cooked material that is kindled upon is clay with which they build buildings. His saying,
h
Then make for me a tower

, means: Build me a building out of bricks, and every flat building is a tower like a palace. And from it the poet said: They are ostriches built by men, so do not think their landmarks are towers. It means by towers: plural of tower. And his saying,
h
Perhaps I may look upon the God of Moses

, means: I look upon the God of Moses, whom he worships and calls others to worship. And I think, in what he says, that he has a God whom he worships in heaven, and that he is the one who supports and aids him, and that he is the one who sent him to us from among the liars. So he mentioned to us that Haman built the tower for him, and he climbed over it.

c: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said:
m: Pharaoh said to his people, “O eminent ones, I know of no god for you other than me. So kindle for me, O Haman, a fire of clay and build for me a tower,” so that I may go into the heavens and see the god of Moses. When the tower was built for him, he climbed over it and ordered an arrow to be shot towards the heavens, and it returned to him covered in blood. He said, “I have killed the god of Moses. God is far above what they say.”

x: God Almighty says: Pharaoh and his soldiers were too arrogant in the land of Egypt to believe in Moses and follow him in what he called them to of the Oneness of God and the acknowledgment of servitude to Him without right meaning transgression and rebellion against their Lord and they thought that they would not be returned to Us meaning: They thought that after their death they would not be resurrected, nor would there be reward or punishment, so they followed their desires and did not know that God was watching them and that He would punish them for their evil deeds.

And His statement, So We seized him and his soldiers, God Almighty says: So We gathered Pharaoh and his soldiers from the Copts. And We cast them into the sea, meaning: So We threw them all into the sea and drowned them in it, as Abu al-Aswad al-Du’ali said: I looked at his address and discarded it as I would discard a worn-out sandal from yours.
He mentioned that it is a sea behind Egypt, as:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So We cast them into the sea. He said: The sea was a sea called Isaf, beyond Egypt, and God drowned them in it. And His statement, Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers, God Almighty says: So look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart: how was the case of those who wronged themselves, who disbelieved in their Lord and rejected the advice of His Messenger. Did We not destroy them and leave their homes and their wealth to Our allies, and grant them what they had of gardens, springs, treasures, and a noble station, after they had been oppressed, their sons killed and their women kept alive? So we will do the same to you and to those who believed in you and confirmed you. We will grant you and them homes from your lie, and return to you what you brought them of the truth and their wealth, and destroy them by killing with the sword. This is the way of God with those who passed on before.

x: God Almighty says: And We made Pharaoh and his people leaders whom the people of rebellion against God and disbelief in Him would follow. They called people to the deeds of the people of the Fire. And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped. God Almighty says: And on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped if a helper punishes them. They used to help one another in this world, but that help vanished on that day.
And His statement,
h
And We pursued them with a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection

, God Almighty says: And We imposed upon Pharaoh and his people in this world disgrace and wrath from Us upon them, so We inevitably decreed for them therein destruction, ruin, and bad praise, and We will pursue them with another curse on the Day of Resurrection, so We will disgrace them with it with permanent disgrace, and humiliate them with the necessary humiliation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of the one who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And We pursued them in this world with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection
. He said: They were cursed in this world and the Hereafter. He said: It is like His saying, “
h
And they were pursued in this world with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection
. What an evil provision it is!” (Hu: 99).

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We pursued them in this world with a curse and on the Day of Resurrection
, meaning another curse. Then he switched gears and said,
h
They are among the despised
. And his statement,
h
They are among the despised

, means, the Most High says: They are among the people whom God deemed ugly, so He destroyed them for their disbelief in their Lord and their denial of His Messenger Moses, peace be upon him. So He made them an example for those who reflect and a lesson for those who take heed.

x: God Almighty says: “And We had certainly given Moses the Torah after We had destroyed the nations that were before him, such as the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and the people of Midian. “As insights for the people” meaning: light for the Children of Israel regarding what they needed in their religious affairs. And guidance meaning: clarification for them and mercy for those of them who acted upon it. That they might remember meaning: so that they might remember God’s blessings upon them with that, so that they might thank Him for it and not be ungrateful. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement,
h
And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad and Abd al-Wahhab told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Abu Nadra, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, who said:
m: God did not destroy a people with a punishment from the sky or from the earth after He sent down the Torah upon the face of the earth, except for the village that was transformed into monkeys. Have you not seen that God says:
h
And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations
as insight for the people and guidance and mercy that they might be reminded.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace:
h
And you were not

, O Muhammad, on the side of the west of the mountain when We decreed the matter to Moses meaning: when We imposed the matter on Moses regarding what We obligated him and his people to do, and We entrusted him with a covenant.
h
And you were not
among the witnesses meaning:
h
and you were not
among the witnesses to that. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And you were not
, O Muhammad, on the western side, he says: on the western side of the mountain, when We decreed to Moses the command.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: To the west of the mountain.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ad-Dahhak bin Mukhallad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ali bin Mudrik, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Amr, who said:
m: You, the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been answered before you were asked. And he recited:
h
And you were not
on the western side when We gave Moses the command.

x: God Almighty means by His saying,
h
But We created generations
, but We created nations and then brought them into existence after that, so life was prolonged for them. And His saying,
h
And you were not residing among the people of Madyan
, means:
h
And you were not residing among the people of Madyan

. It is said: I resided in a place, I reside there, a dwelling. A’sha Tha’labah said: He stayed and shortened his night to provide for them, so he went and broke his appointment with the one killed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And you were not a resident among the people of Madyan

, he said: Residing means reciting to them Our verses, meaning: you read to them Our book, but We were messengers, meaning: You did not witness any of that, O Muhammad, but we were the ones who did that and sent messengers.

x: God Almighty says: And you, O Muhammad, were not beside the mountain when We called to Moses, saying, I will prescribe it for those who fear God and give zakat and those who believe in Our verses * who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet (al-A’raf 7:156-157)....

c: As Isa bin Othman bin Isa Al-Ramli told us, he said: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ali bin Mudrik, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
And you were not beside the mountain when We called out
, he said: He called out, O nation of Muhammad, I gave to you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you were not beside the mountain when We called out
, he said: They were called out: O nation of Muhammad, I gave to you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told me, he said: Harmalah bin Qais Al-Nakha’i told us, he said:
m: I heard this hadith from Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir, on the authority of Abu Hurairah,
h
And you were not beside the mountain when We called out
, he said: They were called out, O nation of Muhammad, I gave to you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Mu’tamir narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman,
m: and Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman, and Hajjaj, on the authority of Hamza Al-Zayyat, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ali bin Mudrik, on the authority of Abu Zur’ah bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding His statement,
h
And you were not beside the Mount when We called out

, he said: They were called out, O nation of Muhammad, I gave to you before you asked Me, and I answered you before you called upon Me. He said: And this is His statement when Moses said, And decree for us in this world [that which is] good and in the Hereafter... the verse. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: something similar. And His statement,
h
But as a mercy from your Lord

, the Most High says: You did not witness any of that, O Muhammad, so you would know it, but We made it known to you, and revealed it to you, and We related all of that to you in Our Book, and We sent you with what We sent down to you of that as a Messenger to whomever We sent you to from among the creation, as a mercy from Us to you and to them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: But it is a mercy from your Lord that We have related to you that you may warn a people... the verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: But a mercy from your Lord. He said: It was a mercy from your Lord that was the prophecy. And His statement,
h
That you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you

, means, Almighty and Majestic is He: But We have sent you with this Book and this religion to warn a people to whom no warner had come before you, and they are the Arabs to whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent. God sent him to them as a mercy to warn them of His punishment for their worship of idols and their associating other gods and rivals with Him. His saying, Perhaps they will remember, means: So that they may remember the error of what they are doing, their disbelief in their Lord, so that they may return to acknowledging God’s Oneness and worshipping Him alone, without all other gods besides Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, But mercy from your Lord he said: What We sent down to you of the Qur’an
h
that you may warn a people to whom no warner had come before you

x: God the Almighty says: And had it not been that these people to whom I have sent you, O Muhammad, would say, “If Our punishment had befallen them, or Our torment had come to them before We sent you to them, because of their disbelief in their Lord, their acquisition of sins, and their commission of transgressions, ‘Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger before Your wrath befalls us and Your torment descends upon us, so that we might follow Your proofs and the verses of Your Book which You sent down to Your Messenger and be among the believers in Your divinity, who confirm Your Messenger in what You have commanded us and forbidden us,’ We would have hastened the punishment upon them for their polytheism before We sent you to them. But We sent you to them as a warner of Our punishment for their disbelief, so that mankind would have no argument against God after the messengers.” The calamity in this context is the punishment and the vengeance. What is meant by because of what their hands have put forth is what they have earned.

God Almighty says: So when there came to them, to whom no warner had come before you, O Muhammad, We sent you as a warner, the truth from Us, that is, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, with the message from God to them, they said, rebelling against God and persisting in their error: Why was not this one who was sent to us, that is, Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, given the like of what was given to Moses, son of Imran, of the Book? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Say, O Muhammad, to your people from Quraysh, who say to you, Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses? Or did those among the Jews who knew this argument not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before you? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The Jews ordered the Quraysh to ask Muhammad for the same as what was given to Moses. God said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell the Quraysh to say to them: Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: They said, ‘Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?’ He said: The Jews commanded the Quraysh, then he mentioned something similar They said, Two magicians conspired. The reciters differed in their recitation of this verse. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as they said, Two magicians cooperated meaning: Or did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?
h
And they said

to him and to Muhammad (peace be upon him) according to some of the commentators, and according to some of them to Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them), and according to some of them to Jesus and Muhammad, Two magicians cooperated Al-Kufa’. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as they said, Two magicians cooperated meaning:
h
And they said
to the Torah and the Criterion according to some of the commentators, and according to some of them to the Gospel and the Criterion.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, according to the difference in the readers’ reading of it. It was mentioned that he said: The two magicians who conspired were Muhammad and Moses, peace be upon them.

c: Sulayman ibn Muhammad ibn Ma’di Karib al-Ra’ini told us: Baqiyah ibn al-Walid told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, who said:
m: I heard Muslim ibn Yasar narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the statement of God two magicians who backed each other up, he said: Moses and Muhammad.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, who said:
m: I heard Muslim ibn Yasar say: I asked Ibn Abbas about this verse Two magicians who conspired against one another, he said: Moses and Muhammad.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Kaysan Abu Hamza, on the authority of Muslim bin Yasar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same. Who said: Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Two magicians who conspired against each other, he said: The Jews against Moses and Aaron.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid They
m: said, Two magicians have conspired the words of the Jews to Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them.

c: Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us: Ismail ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr and Abu Razin,
m: that one of them read two magicians who conspired against one another, and the other: two magicians. The one who read two magicians said: The Torah and the Gospel. The one who read two magicians said: Moses and Aaron.
b.via: Saeed ibn Jubayr and Abu Razin

x: Others said that by the magicians they meant Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: his statement two magicians who conspired he said: Jesus and Muhammad, or he said: Moses, peace be upon him. It was mentioned that those who said: They meant by that the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion, and he directed its interpretation to the reading of those who read
h
Two magicians who supported each other

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Two magicians who supported each other
means: the Torah and the Qur’an.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: They said, ‘Two magicians have supported each other.’ Meaning: the Torah and the Criterion.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, They said, ‘
h
Two magicians who supported each other

,’ he said: The book of Moses, and the book of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was mentioned that they meant the Torah and the Gospel. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, on the authority of Humayd al-A’raj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was next to Ibn Abbas while he was seeking refuge between the Corner and the Station of Prayer. I said: How do you recite Two magicians or Two magicians? He did not answer me. Then Ikrimah said: Two magicians, and I thought that if he disliked that, he would have denied it to me. Humayd said: Then I met Ikrimah after that and mentioned that to him and said: How did he recite it? He said: He used to recite
h
Two magicians who supported each other
, meaning the Torah and the Gospel. It was mentioned that they meant the Criterion and the Gospel.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: that he recited, Two magicians supported each other, meaning the Gospel and the Criterion.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, They said, ‘Two magicians who support each other.’ That was said by the enemies of God, the Jews, regarding the Gospel and the Criterion. So whoever says, Two magicians, says, Muhammad and Jesus, son of Mary.

x: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of those who read it, They said, ‘Two magicians supported each other,’ meaning: the book of Moses, which is the Torah, and the book of Jesus, which is the Gospel. We said: This is the more correct of the two readings, because the speech before it was about the Book, which is His statement, They said, ‘Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?’ And what follows it after it is about the Book, which is His statement,
h
Then bring a Book from God that is a better guide than both of them

, and I will follow it. So what is between them, that it was mentioned, is more appropriate and more likely to be mentioned other than it. And since this is the more correct reading, it is known that the meaning of the speech is: Say, O Muhammad, did these Jews not disbelieve in what Moses was given before, and say, What Moses was given of the Book and what you were given is two magics that cooperated.
And His statement,
h
And they said
, ‘We disbelieve in all of them.’ God Almighty says: The Jews said, We disbelieve in every book on earth, including the Torah, the Gospel, the Psalms, and the Criterion.
Some of the interpreters said something similar to what we said about this, and others disagreed with him on this.
Mention of someone who said the same as we said about that:

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, we disbelieve in all of it, they said: We also disbelieve in what Muhammad was given.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
And they said
, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in all of it.’ The Jews also said: We disbelieve in what Muhammad was given as well.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is:
h
And they said
, We disbelieve in both the Qur’an and the Gospel.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And they said
, ‘We disbelieve in all of them.’ He said: in the Gospel and the Qur’an.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And they said
, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them.’ They meant the Gospel and the Criterion.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And they said

, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in all Surat al-Qasas 28:48 So when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?" And did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, "Two magicians conspired together,"
h
and they said
, "Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them." of them.’ He said: They are the People of the Book, meaning: in the two books: the Torah and the Criterion.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And they said
, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in all of them,’ which was brought by Moses, and which was brought by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this verse.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it as they said, Two magicians cooperated meaning: Or did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?

The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as they said, Two magicians cooperated meaning: And they said to the Torah and the Criterion according to some of the commentators, and according to some of them to the Gospel and the Criterion.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, according to the difference in the readers’ reading of it.

It was mentioned that those who said: They meant by that the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion, and he directed its interpretation to the reading of those who read Two magicians who supported each other.
Humayd said: Then I met Ikrimah after that and mentioned that to him and said: How did he recite it?

Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading of those who read it, They said, ‘Two magicians supported each other,’ meaning: the book of Moses, which is the Torah, and the book of Jesus, which is the Gospel.
We said: This is the more correct of the two readings, because the speech before it was about the Book, which is His statement, They said, ‘Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given?’

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say about the Torah and the Gospel: They are two magics that pretend to be magic: Bring a book from God that is a better guide than them to the path of truth and to the way of right conduct. I will follow it, if you should be truthful in your claim that these two books are magic, and that the truth is in something else. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God Almighty said:
m: “Say: Then bring a book from God that is better guidance than both of them”... the verse. Yunus narrated: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: God said, Bring me a book from God that is better guidance than these two books, which was sent by Moses and which was sent by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: God the Most High says: If these Jews, O Muhammad, who say that the Torah and the Gospel are two forms of magic, who claim that the truth is in other than them, do not answer you until they bring you a book from God that is better guidance than them, then know that they are only following their own desires and that what they utter and say about the two books is a lie and a falsehood that has no truth to it. Perhaps someone might say: Did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, not know that what the Jews and others said about the Torah and the Gospel of slander and falsehood, who call them two forms of magic, is falsehood unless they do not answer him until they bring you a book that is better guidance than them? It was said: This is a statement that was addressed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it is the one to whom it was said: Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before from the disbelievers of Quraysh?

That is because it was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:Did not these people who commanded you to say: Why was Muhammad not given something like Moses? disbelieve in what Moses was given before, this Qur’an, and say about what was revealed to him and to Jesus: Two magicians who backed up each other? So say to them: If you are truthful that what Moses and Jesus were given was magic, then bring me a book from God that is better guidance than their two books. If they do not respond to that, then know that they are liars, and that they only follow in their denial of Muhammad and what he brought them from God their own desires, and they abandon the truth while they know. God Almighty says: And who is more astray from the path of guidance and the path of righteousness than he who follows his own desire without clarification from God and a covenant from God, and abandons the covenant of God which He made to His creation in His revelation.

And His revelation: Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people. God Almighty says: Indeed, God does not guide to the truth and the path of right guidance the people who disobeyed God’s command, abandoned His obedience, denied His Messenger, changed His covenant, and followed their own desires, preferring obedience to Satan over obedience to their Lord.

God Almighty says: And We have certainly conveyed to your people from Quraysh and to the Jews from the Children of Israel the report of the past and the information about what We brought upon them of Our punishment, when they denied Our messengers, and about what We will do to those who follow in their footsteps and imitate their example in disbelief in God and in denying His messengers, so that they may remember and take heed and learn a lesson.

i: Its origin is from joining ropes together, and from it is the saying of the poet:
x: So tell the Banu Marwan, what is the matter with the covenant and the weak rope that keeps on connecting?
And similar to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, although their wording differed in their explanation of its interpretation.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: We explained. And some of them said: Its meaning is: We separated.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Waki’i told us: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, And We have certainly detailed the word to them, meaning, We have detailed the word to them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word
He said: God conveyed to them the Word in this Qur’an, informing them of how He dealt with those who have passed away, and how He will deal, that they may remember.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Muhammad bin Isa Abu Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin ʿUyaynah:
m: It reached us: We were told.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We have certainly connected to them the report, the report of this world with the report of the Hereafter, until it was as if they had witnessed the Hereafter and witnessed it in this world, with what We show them of signs in this world and the like. And he recited, Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter
r

and said: Indeed, We will fulfill for them what We promised them in the Hereafter, just as We fulfilled for the prophets what We promised them. We will judge between them and their people. The commentators differed as to who was meant by the ha and mim in his statement, And We have certainly connected them.

x: Some of them said: He meant Quraysh by them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word
, he said: Quraysh.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And We have certainly conveyed to them the word, he said: to the Quraysh.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word that perhaps they will be reminded
, he said, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: He meant the Jews.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Adam told me, he said: Affan bin Muslim told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, he said: Amr bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Ja’dah, on the authority of Rifa’ah Al-Qurazi, he said:
m: This verse was revealed about ten people, and I was one of them:
h
And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word that perhaps they will be reminded

c: Ibn Sinan told us: Hayyan told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ja'dah, on the authority of Atiyyah al-Qurazi, who said:
m: This verse, And We have certainly continued to them the Word that they may be reminded, was revealed until it reached, Indeed, we were Muslims before this, about ten, one of whom was me. So it is as if Ibn Abbas meant by his statement, meaning Muhammad, that perhaps they would remember God's covenant with them concerning Muhammad, so they would acknowledge his prophethood and believe in him. And His statement, Those to whom We gave the Scripture before this - they believe in it, means by this the Most High, the Most Glorious, a group of the People of the Scripture who believed in His Messenger and confirmed him. So He said, Those to whom We gave the Scripture before this Qur’an - they believe in this Qur’an, so they acknowledge that it is the truth from God, and the ignorant, unlettered ones who did not receive the Scripture from God are liars. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the Almighty’s statement,
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it
. He said: It means those who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the People of the Book.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it are content with it .... to His saying, We do not seek the ignorant in the Muslims of the People of the Scripture.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it… to His statement, the ignorant, he said: They are the Muslims among the People of the Scripture. Ibn Jurayj said: Amr ibn Dinar informed me that Yahya ibn Ja’dah informed him, on the authority of Ali ibn Rifa’ah, who said: Ten men from among the People of the Scripture went out to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and among them was Abu Rifa’ah, meaning his father, and they believed, but they were harmed, so Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it was revealed before the Qur’an.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it

. He said: We were told that it was revealed about people from the People of the Scripture who were on a path of truth, taking it and adhering to it, until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they believed in him and confirmed his truth, so God gave them their reward twice, for their patience with the first Scripture, and their following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their patience with that. He mentioned that among them were Salman and Abdullah bin Salam.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement,
h
Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it

... to His statement, before it, Muslims: People from the People of the Scripture believed in the Torah and the Gospel, then they lived to see Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believed in him, so God gave them their reward twice for their patience: by their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, and by their following him when he was sent. That is what His statement, Indeed, we were Muslims before him.

x: God Almighty says: And when this Qur’an is recited to those to whom We gave the Scripture before the revelation of this Qur’an, they say, We believe in it. That is, they say, We believe in it. “Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord.” That is, it was revealed from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before the revelation of this Qur’an. This is because they believed in what the prophets brought before the coming of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they had the Scriptures, and in their Scriptures were the description and attributes of Muhammad, so they believed in him, his mission, and his Scripture before the revelation of the Qur’an. That is why they said, Indeed, we were Muslims before it.

evidence.text: God Almighty says: And when this Qur’an is recited to those to whom We gave the Scripture before the revelation of this Qur’an, they say, We believe in it.

x: God Almighty says: These are the ones whose characteristics I have described, they will be given the reward for their deeds twice because of their patience.
The interpreters of the Qur'an differed over the meaning of the patience for which God promised what He promised.

Some of them said: He promised them what He, the Most High, promised, for their patience with the first scripture, their following of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their patience in that. This is the opinion of Qatada, and we have mentioned it previously.

Others said: Rather, He promised them patience through their belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, and through their following him when he was sent. This is the statement of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, which we also mentioned before. Among those who agreed with Qatada on his statement was Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, we were Muslims before him, in the religion of Jesus. Then when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, they became Muslims, and they had their reward twice: for their patience the first time, and they entered Islam with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some people said about this:

c: Ibn Wakee’ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: A people who were polytheists converted to Islam, but their people used to harm them, so the following verse was revealed: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured. And His statement:
h
And they repel evil with good

means: And they repel evil with the good deeds that they do. And from what We have provided them of wealth they spend in obedience to God, either in jihad in the way of God, or in charity to the needy, or in maintaining kinship ties.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement, “And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it.’” God said, Those will be given their reward twice over for what they patiently endured. And God praised them well, as you hear, and said,
h
And they repel evil with good

evidence.text: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, “And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it.

x: God Almighty says: And when these people to whom We gave the Scripture hear: vain talk, which is false speech.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And when they hear ill speech
, they turn away from it and say, ‘To us our deeds, and to you your deeds.
h
Peace be upon you
. We seek not the ignorant.’” They do not go along with the people of ignorance and falsehood in their falsehood. God’s command came to them and they did not turn away from that.

x: Others said: What is meant by idleness in this context is what the People of the Book added to the Book of God, which is not part of it.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And when they hear ill speech

, they turn away from it and say… to the end of the verse, he said: This is for the People of the Book, when they hear ill speech that the people have written with their own hands along with the Book of God, and they say: It is from God, when those who have become Muslims hear it and pass by it reciting it, they turn away from it, and it is as if they had not heard that before they believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they were Muslims following the religion of Jesus. Do you not see that they say: Indeed, we were Muslims before him.

x: Others said about this:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And when they hear ill speech
, they turn away from it and say, ‘To us our deeds, and to you your deeds.
h
Peace be upon you
.’” He said: It was revealed about a people who were polytheists and then converted to Islam, but their people used to harm them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Juwayriyah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And when they hear ill speech

, they turn away from it and say, ‘For us our deeds, and for you your deeds.’ He said: There were people from the People of the Book who converted to Islam, and the polytheists used to harm them, but they would forgive them, saying, “
h
Peace be upon you

. We do not seek the ignorant.” His statement, They turned away from him, means they did not listen to him or hear him. And they said, ‘For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds.’ This indicates that the idle talk that God mentioned in this place is what Mujahid said, that it was the people hearing from those who hurt them with words that they disliked from them in themselves, and that they responded to them with beautiful words, For us are our deeds, that they were pleased with them for themselves, and for you are your deeds, that they were pleased with them for yourselves. His statement, “
h
Peace be upon you

,” means that it is a protection for you from us that we should not insult you, or that you should hear from us what you do not like. We do not seek the ignorant, that is, we do not want to debate and insult the ignorant.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: “Indeed, O Muhammad, you do not guide whom you love, but God guides whom He wills, by granting them success in believing in Him and in His Messenger. If it were said: Its meaning is: You do not guide whom you love, because of his kinship to you, but God guides whom He wills, that would be an incorrect approach. “
h
And He knows best who are guided

”: God the Almighty says: And God knows best who is guided to the right path, that is the one whom God guides, directs, and grants success. He mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because his uncle Abu Talib refused to answer him when he called him to believe in God and to what he called him to.
The narration mentioned that:

c: Abu Kurayb and Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us: Al-Walid bin Al-Qasim told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Kaysan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his uncle when he was dying: ‘Say there is no god but God, and I will bear witness to it for you on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said: ‘Were it not that the Quraysh would taunt me, I would have made you happy.’ Then God revealed: ‘Indeed, you do not guide whom you love…’… the verse.”

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Kaysan, who said: Abu Hazim al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his uncle: Say, ‘There is no god but God.’ Then he mentioned something similar.”

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Kaysan,
m: who heard Abu Hazim al-Ashja’i mentioning on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: “When the death of Abu Talib was approaching, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and said: ‘O my uncle, say there is no god but God.’ He said something similar, except that he said: ‘Were it not that the Quraysh would taunt me, saying: Nothing made him do it except the fear of death.’”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Kaysan, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Abu Kurayb al-Sada’i.

c: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us: My uncle Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to me: Yunus narrated to me, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: who narrated to me: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me, on the authority of his father, who said: “When Abu Talib was about to die, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and found Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O uncle, say ‘there is no god but God’, a word that I will bear witness for you before God.’ Abu Jahl and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya said: ‘O Abu Talib, do you turn away from the religion of Abdul Muttalib?’” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept presenting it to him and repeating that statement to him, until Abu Talib said the last thing he said to them: He follows the religion of Abdul Muttalib, and he refused to say there is no god but God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so. Then God revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives (al-Tawbah 9:113). And God revealed about Abu Talib, and he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, but God guides … the verse.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us,
m: on the Surat al-Qasas 28:56 Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided. authority of Amr, on the authority of Abu Saeed bin Rafi’, who said: I said to Ibn Umar: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love was revealed about Abu Talib? He said: Yes.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, he said: Muhammad’s statement to Abu Talib, Say the word of sincerity, and I will argue for you with it on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad ibn Amr said in his hadith: He said: O my nephew, the religion of the elders, or the way of the elders. Al-Harith said in his hadith: He said, O my nephew, the religion of the ghosts.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love. He said: Muhammad said to Abu Talib, Bear witness to the word of sincerity, and I will argue for you with it on the Day of Resurrection. He said: That is, my nephew, the religion of the elders. So God revealed, Indeed, you do not guide whom you love. He said: This verse was revealed about Abu Talib.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Indeed, you do not guide whom you love, it was mentioned to us that it was revealed about Abu Talib. Al-Asam said, when he was dying, he said, There is no god but God, so that intercession would be permitted for him, but he refused. Ibn Humayd narrated: Jarir narrated from Ata’ from Amir: “When Abu Talib was about to die, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘O my uncle, say, ‘There is no god but God,’ and I will bear witness for you with it on the Day of Resurrection.’ He said to him: ‘O my nephew, were it not for the shame on you, I would not mind doing so.’ He said that to him repeatedly. When he died, the matter became very difficult for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: ‘The kinship of Abu Talib will not benefit you.’ He said: ‘Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, he will be in the shallows of Hellfire at this moment, wearing two sandals of boiling fire from which his head will boil. There is no person among the people of Hellfire whose punishment is lighter than him.’ He is the one about whom God revealed: ‘Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.’” And His saying,
h
And He knows best who are guided
, means: And He knows best who has been guided.

c: Like what Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And He is most knowing of the guided ones
, he said of those for whom guidance and misguidance have been decreed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: God Almighty says: The infidels of Quraysh said: If we follow the truth that you have brought us with you, and disavow our rivals and gods, the people will snatch us from our land with the unanimous agreement of all of them to disagree with us and fight us. God says to His Prophet: Say, Have We not established for them a sanctuary? He says: Did We not establish for them a land in which We have forbidden the people to shed blood, and prevented them from harming its inhabitants, and guaranteed security for its people from being afflicted there by a raid, or killing, or captivity? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that Al-Harith bin Nawfal, who said, If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched from our land, and they claimed that they said: We know that you are the Messenger of God, but we fear that we will be snatched from our land, Did We not establish them?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And they said

, ‘If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.’ He said: They were people from Quraysh who said to Muhammad, If we follow you, the people will snatch us away. So God said,
h
Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary
to which are brought the fruits of all things?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement and people are snatched away from around them, he said: Some of them would attack others. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement,
h
Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary
? the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they said
, ‘If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land,’ God said,
h
Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary
to which are brought the fruits of all kinds? He says: Were they not secure in their sanctuary, neither raiding it nor fearing, to which are brought the fruits of all kinds?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told me, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary

? He said: The people of the sanctuary were safe and could go whenever they wanted. If one of them went out and said: I am one of the people of the sanctuary, no one would interfere with him. But if anyone other than them went out, he would be killed.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Did We not establish for them a secure sanctuary
? He said: We made you secure in it. He said: It is Mecca, and they are Quraysh. His statement,
h
The fruits of everything are brought to it

, means that they are gathered to it. This is from their saying, I gathered the water in the basin, meaning I collected it in it. What is meant by this is: the fruits of every country are brought to it.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi Zar’ah, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding The fruits of all things are brought to Him, he said: The fruits of the earth. And His statement,
h
A provision from Us

, means: And a provision We have provided them from Us, meaning: from Us. But most of them do not know, means: God Almighty says: But most of these polytheists who say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land, do not know that it is We who established for them a secure sanctuary, and provided for them in it, and made the fruits of every land be collected for them. So, due to their ignorance of the One who did that to them, they are ungrateful and do not thank the One who bestowed that blessing upon them. Surat al-Qasas 28:57
h
And they said
, "If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land."
h
Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary
to which are brought the fruits of all things as provision from Us? But most of them do not know.

x: God Almighty says: And how many a town have We destroyed which was made arrogant by its livelihood, so it became insolent, wicked, and transgressed, and denied its Lord.
