It was also said: its livelihood became arrogant, so the verb was given to the town, although it is originally for livelihood, just as it is said: your opinion made you foolish, so you made it foolish, and your wealth made you arrogant, so you made it arrogant. Livelihood is in the accusative case as an explanation. We have explained similar examples in more than one place in this book. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And how many a city have We destroyed which was insolent in its life

, he said: Insolence is the worst of the heedless, the people of falsehood, and those who ride the sins of God. He said: That is insolence in blessings. Then those were their dwellings; they were not inhabited after them except a little, meaning: Those were the homes of the people whom We destroyed for their disbelief in their Lord and their dwellings; they were not inhabited after them except a little. He said: They were ruined after them, and only a small part of them was inhabited, and most of them were ruined. The wording of the statement, even if it is based on the fact that their dwellings were inhabited only a little, its meaning is: Those were their dwellings; they were not inhabited after them except a little, just as one says: I fulfilled your right except a little of it. And His statement:
h
And We were the inheritors

means: And what We destroyed of their dwellings had no heir among them, and they returned to what they had been before they had lived in them, with no owner but God, to whom belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth.

x: God Almighty says: And your Lord would not destroy the towns around Mecca in your time and age until He sends to its mother a messenger meaning: until He sends to Mecca a messenger, which is the mother of towns, who recites to them the verses of Our Book, and the messenger is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in a manner similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until He sends a messenger to its mother, and the mother of villages is Mecca, and God sent to them a messenger: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement,
h
And We would not destroy cities except while their people were wrongdoers

, means: We would not destroy a city while it believed in God. We would only destroy it because of its wrongdoing to itself and its disbelief in God. We only destroyed the people of Mecca because of their disbelief in their Lord and their wrongdoing to themselves. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And We would not destroy the towns except while their people were wrongdoers

. God said: He did not destroy a town because of faith, but He destroys the towns because of wrongdoing when their people were wrongdoers. Had they believed, they would not have been destroyed with those who were destroyed, but they lied and were wrongdoers, and so they were destroyed because of that.

x: God Almighty says: Whatever you have been given, O people, of wealth and children, is only a provision that you enjoy in this worldly life, and it is from its adornments with which people adorn themselves. It will not avail you at all with God, nor will it benefit you in your afterlife. What is with God for the people of His obedience and allegiance is better and more lasting than what you have been given in this world of its provision and adornments, and it is more lasting for its people, because it is eternal and will never end. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And what is with God is better and more lasting

, he said: Better in reward and more lasting with us. Do you not then understand? God Almighty says: O people, do you not have minds with which to reflect and know good from evil, and choose for yourselves the better of the two positions over the worse of them, and prefer the everlasting, endless bliss over the transient, unlasting one?

x: God Almighty says: Is he to whom We have promised Paradise for his obedience to Us, and he believed in what We promised him, and was truthful and obeyed Us, and thus deserved, through his obedience to Us, that We should fulfill for him what We promised him, and he will attain what he was promised and become a god, like one to whom We have given enjoyment in the life of this world, and he enjoyed it, and forgot to do what We promised the people of obedience, and abandoned seeking it, and preferred immediate pleasure to a deferred one, then on the Day of Resurrection he will be visited by those brought before God, meaning those who are present, the punishment of God and His painful chastisement. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Is he to whom We have promised a good promise which he will surely attain

? He said: He is the believer who heard the Book of God, believed in it, and believed in what God promised in it. Like he to whom We have given enjoyment of worldly life. He is this disbeliever. By God, he is not like the believer. Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth. That is, in the punishment of God.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Ibn Amr said in his hadith: His statement, among those brought forth, he said: They brought her. Al-Harith said in his hadith, Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth, the people of Hell, they brought her forth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth. He said: The people of Hell will be brought forth.

x: The interpreters differed about who this verse was revealed about.
Some of them said: It was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Hakam bin Abdullah Al-Ajli told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Taghlib, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise which he will attain like he to whom We have given enjoyment of worldly life and then, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be among those brought forth? He said: It was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about Abu Jahl bin Hisham.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise which he will surely fulfill? He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Others said: It was revealed about Hamza and Ali, may God be pleased with them, and Abu Jahl, may God curse him.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Badal bin Al-Muhabbir Al-Taghlabi told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abaan bin Taghlib, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise which he will attain like he to whom We have given enjoyment of worldly life and then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth? He said: It was revealed about Hamza, Ali bin Abi Talib, and Abu Jahl. He said: Abd al-Samad told us, he said:

c: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abaan ibn Taghlib, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: It was revealed about Hamza and Abu Jahl.

x: God Almighty says: And on the Day the Lord of Majesty will call out to those with whom they associated rivals and idols in this world, and He will say to them: Where are My partners whom you claimed that they were My partners in this world?

Those upon whom the word was justified said, meaning: Those upon whom God's wrath and curse were due, and they were the devils who misled the children of Adam, said: "Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray. We led them astray just as we were led astray." And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
These are the ones whom We led astray

, We led them astray just as We were led astray, he said: They are the devils. His saying: We disavow you means: We disavow their allegiance and support to you. They did not worship us means: They did not worship us.

x: God Almighty says: And it will be said to those who associate others with God, the gods and rivals in this world, Call upon your partners whom you used to call upon besides God. So they called upon them, but they did not respond to them. He says: They did not answer them. And they saw the punishment He says: And they witnessed the punishment. If only they had been guided. He says: When they saw the punishment, they wished that they had been guided to the truth in this world.

God Almighty says: And on the Day God will call these polytheists and say to them: What did you answer the messengers? regarding what We sent them to you with, of calling you to our monotheism and disavowing idols and statues.

And the report was hidden from them that Day: He says: So the report was hidden from them, from their saying: The report of the people was hidden from me, meaning it was concealed. What is meant by that is that the argument was hidden from them, so they did not know what to use as evidence for, because God Almighty had been more eloquent in his apology to them, and had continued the argument against them, so they had no argument to use as evidence, nor any report to tell, which would be a means of salvation and deliverance for them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, So the report was hidden from them, he said: The arguments, meaning the proof.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: So the report was hidden from them. He said: The arguments. He said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement: And the Day He will call to them and say, ‘What was your response to the messengers?’ He said: There is no god but God, monotheism. And his saying: They do not ask about lineages and kinship.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They do not ask one another he said: They do not ask one another about lineage, nor do they seek to know one another about kinship. They used to ask one another about one another when they met in this world, and they would die together.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: So they will not ask each other about lineages. He said: About lineages. It was said that the meaning of this is: So the arguments were hidden from them on that day, so they remained silent. So they will not ask each other about them while they are silent.

x: God Almighty says: But as for he who repents from among the polytheists, who turns back and returns to the truth, and sincerely devotes divinity to God, and singles out worship for Him, so he does not associate anything with Him in his worship, and believes meaning: and believes in His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. and does righteousness meaning: and does what God has commanded him to do in His Book, and on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, then perhaps he will be among the successful meaning: he is among the successful who attain what they seek from God, who will remain eternally in His Paradise, and perhaps is obligatory from God.

God Almighty says: And your Lord O Muhammad creates what He wills to create, and chooses for His guardianship the best of His creation, and those who have been destined for happiness from among them. And God Almighty said: and chooses what was best for them and the meaning is: what I described, because the polytheists, as was mentioned about them, chose their wealth, and allocated it to their gods. So God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And your Lord, O Muhammad, creates what He wills to create, and chooses for guidance and righteous deeds from among His creation what He knew was best of them, similar to what these polytheists did for their gods, the best of their wealth. So too is My choice for Myself, and My selection for My guardianship, and My selection for My service and obedience, the best of My kingdom and My creation. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: "
h
And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses

. It is not for them to choose." He said: They used to give the best of their wealth to their gods in the Age of Ignorance. So if the meaning of that is thus, then there is no doubt that ma in His statement and chooses what is not for them to choose is in the accusative case, because yachooth is placed on it, and that it means who.

x: If the matter was described, that what is a noun in the accusative case because of the occurrence of his saying: chooses upon it, then where is the predicate of was? You have known that if it is as you said, that in was there is a mention of what, and if was is thus there must be a completion, and where is the completion?
The Arabs sometimes make the letters of descriptions, if the predicates come after them, predicates, like their action with nouns if their predicates come after them.

i: Al-Farra’ mentioned that Al-Qasim bin Ma’n recited to him the saying of Antarah:
x: I hope my tears flow, if that had been known to you before today So he raised the known with the letter of description, and it is undoubtedly the predicate of that, and it was mentioned that Al-Mufaddal recited this to him: If only you had known this before today And also from it is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabia: I said answer, a lover who is charged with your love There are three of them: a doll, a virgin, and a loaner.

So, the one who is charged with describing a lover, and he raised it with the letter of description, which is the ba’, in similar to what we mentioned with many examples, so likewise his saying: And they choose what is for them the choice, he raised the choice with the description, and it is for them, even though it is the predicate of what, because it came after the description, and the description took the place of the predicate, so it became like the saying of the one who said: Amr, his father was standing, there is no doubt that if standing was in the place of the father, and the father was the one who came after him, it would be accusative, so likewise the way of raising the choice, and it is the predicate of what.

Is it permissible for ma in this position to be a denial, and for the meaning of the statement to be: And your Lord creates what He wills to create, and chooses what He wills to choose, so that His statement:
h
And chooses would be the end of the report about creation and choice
, and then the statement after that would be a beginning with the meaning:
h
They had no choice
: that is, creation had no choice, and choice is only for God?

This is a statement whose corruption is not hidden from anyone with reason, for several reasons. If it were not for the statement of the people of interpretation that contradicts it, then how is it when the interpretation of those we mentioned contradicts it? As for one of the aspects of its corruption, it is that if His statement,
h
They had no choice

, were as he thought, that what means denial, in the manner of the interpretation that I mentioned, then the Almighty would have denied that they had any choice in what came before the revelation of this verse. As for what they will have in the future, then they will have any choice, because the statement of the speaker, This was not for you, is undoubtedly a report that he did not have that in the past. It may be permissible for him to have that in the future, and that is undoubtedly a contradiction in speech, because whatever creation did not have of that in the past, then that will never be for them.
And further, if that meaning was intended, then the statement would be: It is not. And it was said:
h
And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses

, they have no choice, so that it would be a negation of that being for them in what came before and what will come after. The second: The Book of God is the clearest in explanation and the most explicit in speech, and it is impossible for anything in it to be unclear in meaning. Surat al-Qasas 28:68
h
And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses

. It is not for them to choose. Glory be to God, and He is far above what they associate with Him. It is not permissible in speech to say at the outset: So-and-so had no choice, when there is a statement before that that implies that. Similarly, His statement: and they choose what was best for them. And before that, there was no report from God, the Most High, about anyone claiming that he had a choice, so it is said to him: You had no choice.

Rather, before that, there was a report about what will happen to those who repent from their polytheism, believe and do righteous deeds. And God, the Most High, followed that with a report about the reason for the faith of those who believed in Him and did righteous deeds among them, and that this is only because He chose them for faith, and because of the foremost among them who was guided by His knowledge of them. What we have said about that increases the clarity of His statement:
h
And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare

. So He informed that He knows the secrets of His servants and what is apparent, and He chooses for Himself and selects for His obedience those from whom He knows the righteous secret and the pleasing outward behavior. The third: The meaning of choice in this context is choice, which is the thing that is chosen from among the animals, livestock, men, and women.

It is said of it: I was given choice and choice, like omens and omens. It is not by choice. If the choice is what we have described, then it is known that the best of speech is to say: “And your Lord creates what He wills, and chooses what He wills. They did not have the best animal or the best food, or the best man or woman.”
Is it permissible for it to have the meaning of a verbal noun?
No, because if it were a verbal noun, the meaning of the statement would be:
h
And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses

that the best be for them. And if that is its meaning, then it is necessary that the worst of the beasts and livestock should not be for them, and if they do not have the worst of them, then it is necessary that they should not have an owner, and that is something whose error is clear, because the best of them and the worst of them have masters who own them by God’s giving them that ownership, and in that being the case, it is corrupt to direct it to the meaning of a verbal noun. And the Almighty's statement: Above what they associate with Him means that God Almighty is glorifying and exonerating Him, and exalting Him above what the polytheists have attributed to Him of polytheism and the lies and falsehoods they have fabricated about Him. The interpretation of this statement is: Glory be to God and He is exalted above their polytheism. Some Arabic scholars have interpreted it to mean: And He is exalted above what you associate with Him.

evidence.text: Al-Farra’ mentioned that Al-Qasim bin Ma’n recited to him the saying of Antarah: I hope my tears flow, if that had been known to you before today So he raised the known with the letter of description, and it is undoubtedly the predicate of that, and it was mentioned that Al-Mufaddal recited this to him: If only you had known this before today And also from it is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabia: I said answer, a lover who is charged with your love There are three of them: a doll, a virgin, and a loaner.

x: God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, knows what the hearts of His creation conceal. It is derived from the root word ‘akannatu shay’ fi sadri I concealed something in my chest, meaning I concealed it within myself. And ‘akannatu shay’ means I protected it. And what they declare: meaning what they reveal with their tongues and limbs. What He means by that is that He chooses whomever He chooses from among them to believe in Him based on His knowledge of the secrets and hidden aspects of their affairs, and that He chooses the people of goodness and guides them to it, and appoints the people of evil and leaves them alone with it.

And His statement: And He is God, there is no god but Him, God Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is the One Who is worshipped, and none is worthy of worship except Him, and there is no god other than Him whose worship is permissible. To Him is praise in the first meaning in this world and the hereafter. “And His is the judgment,” meaning: And to Him is the judgment between His creation. And to Him you will be returned, meaning: And to Him you will be returned after your death, and He will judge between you with justice.

God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: O people, have you considered if God made the night perpetual for you, with no day following it until the Day of Resurrection? The Arabs say of everything that is continuous and does not end, whether it is ease, affliction, or blessing, that it is eternal. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement: eternally means always, never interrupted.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
If God made the night continuous for you
, he means: always. And His statement:
h
Who is a god other than God who can bring you light

? He says: Who is a god other than the One to whom all things are to be worshipped? He brings you the light of day, so that you may be illuminated by it. Do you not hear? He says: Do you not pay attention to that, and reflect on it so that you may be admonished, and know that your Lord is the One who brings the night and takes away the day if He wills, and if He wills He brings the day and takes away the night, so He bestows His blessings upon you through their difference.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your al-Nas 114:‘Have you considered, O people, if God made the day continuous for you, forever, with no night with it, until the Day of Resurrection, what god could be other than God, who could bring you a night in which to rest, so that you may be settled and calm? Do you not see?’” He says: Do you not see with your eyes the alternation of night and day for you, as a mercy from God to you and an argument from Him against you? So learn from this that worship is only appropriate for the One Who has bestowed that upon you and not others, and for the One Who has the power by which He has distinguished between that.

God Almighty says, And of His mercy to you, O people, He made for you the night and the day and made them different, so He made this night darkness that you may rest therein and be calm and settle down for the comfort of your bodies in it from the fatigue of the activities that you do during the day for your livelihoods. And regarding the ha in His statement, that you may rest therein, there are two views: One: That it is from the mention of the night specifically, and another ha is implied for the day with the desire. The second: That it is from the mention of the night and the day, so the way it is unified, and it is for them, is the way it is unified for them, and it is for them the way it is unified for the Arabs in their saying: Your coming and going hurts me, because coming and going is an action, and an action is unified in its many and few forms. And He made this day a light in which you see, so you use your sight in it for your livelihoods, and seeking His provision that He divided among you with His grace that He bestowed upon you.

And His statement: And perhaps you will be grateful, God Almighty says: And that you may thank Him for His blessing upon you with that. He did that to you so that you would single Him out in thanks, and that you would be sincere in your praise to Him, because no partner shared with Him in His blessing upon you with that. Therefore, He should not have a partner in praising Him for it.

That is, the Most High said: And on the Day your Lord will call out, O Muhammad, to these polytheists and say to them: Where are My partners whom you claimed, O people, in this world that they were My partners?
And His statement:
h
And We will extract from every nation a witness

, and We will bring from every group its witness, who is its prophet who will testify to it regarding what his nation responded to regarding the message that he brought them from God. It was said: And We will extract from His statement: So-and-so extracted with such-and-such an argument, meaning: He brought it and brought it out. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We will extract from every nation a witness
, and its witness is its prophet, who bears witness that he has conveyed the message of his Lord.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
And We will extract from every nation a witness
, he said: a messenger.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. And His statement:
h
Then We said

, ‘Bring your proof.’ He says: So We said to the nation of each prophet among them who rejected his advice and denied what he brought them from their Lord, when their prophet bore witness against them that he had conveyed to them God’s message: Bring your proof. He says: So He said to them: Bring your proof for your associating with God what you used to associate, despite God’s excuse to you through the messengers and His establishing proofs upon you. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: “Then we said: Bring your proof,” meaning your evidence.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Then We said
, ‘Bring forth your proof,’ he said: Your argument for what you used to worship and say.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: So We said, ‘Bring your proof.’ He said: Your proof of what you used to worship. And His statement,
h
And they knew that the truth belongs to God

, means: Then they knew that the conclusive proof against them belongs to God, and that the truth belongs to God, and the truth is His report, so they were certain of a punishment from God for them that would be permanent. And what they used to invent was lost to them, meaning: And what they used to associate with God in this world vanished, and what they used to invent and lie about their Lord was lost, so it did not benefit them there, but rather it harmed them, and their reform is the fire of Hell.

x: God Almighty says, Indeed, Qarun - he is Qarun ibn Yashar ibn Qahath ibn Levi ibn Jacob - was from the people of Moses meaning: he was from the clan of Moses ibn Imran the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was his paternal cousin on his father’s and mother’s side. That is because Qarun is Qarun ibn Yashar ibn Qahath, and Moses is Moses ibn Imran ibn Qahath. This is how Ibn Jurayj attributed him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, Korah was from the people of Moses, he said: His cousin, his father’s nephew, for Korah is the son of Yasfar, this is what Al-Qasim said, but he is Yashar ibn Qahath, and Moses is the son of Umar ibn Qahath, and Umar in Arabic is Imran. As for Ibn Ishaq, then - Ibn Humayd told us:

c: Salamah told us
m: on his authority that Yashar ibn Qahath married Sumayt bint Batawit ibn Barkana ibn Bugshan ibn Ibrahim, and she bore him Imran ibn Yashar and Qarun ibn Yashar. Imran then married Bukhant bint Shmuel ibn Barkana ibn Bugshan ibn Barkana, and she bore him Aaron ibn Imran and Moses ibn Imran, the Chosen One of God and His Prophet. Moses, as Ibn Ishaq mentioned, was the nephew of Qarun, and Qarun was his paternal uncle, his father’s brother from his father and mother. Most of the scholars agree on this point.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, Korah was from the people of Moses, he said: He was Moses’ cousin.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, who said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Qarun was from the people of Moses. We used to say that he was his cousin, his father’s brother, and he was called the enlightened one because of the beauty of his voice when reciting the Torah. But the enemy of God was a hypocrite, just as the Samaritan was a hypocrite, so his transgression destroyed him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses. He said: He was his cousin, but he transgressed against him. He said: Yahya Al-Qattan narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Qarun was the cousin of Moses. He said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Khalid, on the authority of Ibrahim, Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses. He said: He was his cousin.

c: Bishr bin Hilal Al-Sawaaf told me: Jaafar bin Sulayman Al-Dab’i told us, on the authority of Malik bin Dinar, who said: It was reported to me that
m: Moses bin Imran was the cousin of Qarun. His saying, So he transgressed against them, means: He exceeded his limits in his arrogance and tyranny towards them.

x: Some of them said: His aggression against them was due to the extra span he took in the length of his clothes.
Who said that?
Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi, Abu Al-Sa’ib, and Ibn Wakee’ told me:

c: Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab,
m: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he transgressed against them. He said: He added a handspan to their clothing.

x: Others said that his aggression against them was due to his great wealth.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: He only transgressed against them because of his great wealth. And His statement,
h
And We gave him of the treasures the keys of which would burden a band of strong men
, God Almighty says: And We gave Qarun of the treasures of wealth the keys of which, which is the plural of miftah, which is that with which one opens doors.

x: Some of them said: What is meant by keys in this place is the treasuries, to burden the group. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said what we said about the meaning of keys:

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us: Al-A’mash told us on the authority of Khaithamah:
m: The keys of Qarun were carried on sixty mules, each key being the door to a known treasure, the size of a finger made of hide.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah, who said:
m: The keys to Qarun’s treasures were made of hides, each key the size of a finger, each key to a separate treasury. When he rode, the keys were carried on sixty white, white-footed mules.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Khaithamah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Its keys would be a burden for a band of strong men

, he said: We find written in the Gospel: The keys of Qarun and Qarun were sixty bright-eyed, white-footed mules, each key of which was no larger than a finger, each key of which contained a treasure.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The keys were made of camel skin.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The keys were made of camel skin.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And We gave him of the treasures
, the keys of which would burden a band of men. He said: Keys made of hides like the keys of sticks.

x: Some people said: What is meant by the keys in this passage is His treasuries.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Hisham told us: Ismail bin Salim told us, on the authority of Abu Salih,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Its keys would be a burden for a band of men
, he said: Its treasuries could be carried on forty mules.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Hujayr, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: What are its keys? He said: Its containers. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of His statement, to burden the group, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, to burden the group, he said: to burden the group.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, to burden the group means: to be heavy. As for the group, it is the congregation.

x: The people of interpretation differed about the amount of its number that was intended in this place. As for the amount of the number of the group in the speech of the Arabs, we have mentioned it previously with the difference of those who differed about it, and the narration in that, and the evidence for the correct of their saying in that which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
Some of them said: Its keys would have been too much for a group, the amount of whose number was forty men.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Salim, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement, It would be too much for a group of men, he said: Forty men.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It would be a burden for the group. He said: It was mentioned to us that the group is between ten and forty.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
A band of strong men would be too heavy for it
, that they claim that a band is forty men, carrying its keys due to their large number.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We gave him of the treasures
, the keys of which would be a burden to a band of strong men, he said: Forty men.

x: Others said: Sixty. He said: Its keys were carried on sixty mules.

m: Ibn Wakee’ also told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Khaithamah.

x: Others said: It carried between three and ten.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jabir bin Nuh told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: It would be too much for a group of people. He said: A group of people is three.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Jabir bin Nuh told us, he said: Abu Rawq told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: It would be too much for a group of people. He said: A group of people is between three and ten.

x: Others said: It carried between ten and fifteen.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said:
m: Abu Asim told Surat al-Qasas 28:76 Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he oppressed them,
h
and We gave him of the treasures
, the keys of which would burden a band of strong men.
h
When his people said to him
h
Do not rejoice
. Indeed, God does not like the exultant." us, he said:

c: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Its keys would be a burden for a company, he said: A company is between ten and fifteen.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: It would be too much for a group. He said: A group: fifteen men. His saying, those of strength means: those of power. Mujahid said about this:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: those with strength, he said: fifteen.

x: How is it said,
h
And We gave him of the treasures
, the keys of which would burden a band of men, and how are the keys burdensome for a band of men, when it is the band of men that burden them?
The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed on this.
Some of the people of Basra said: The metaphor for that is: The band of strong men would not be able to bear the keys of His blessings.

And it is said in speech: Its rump would be burdensome for it, but it is its rump as a camel burdens its load. He said: The Arabs do something like this. The poet said: I would sacrifice myself, my money and my soul for you, and I will not give you more than I can bear.
Meaning: I would sacrifice myself and my money for myself.

Another said: And she rides horses that are relentless among them, and spears are torn apart by the red spears. The misery of the lost ones is due to spears. He said: And the horses here mean the men. Another of them said, Its keys are not. He said: This is a place where if is hardly used as a beginning. He said: The death you are fleeing from will surely meet you. And his saying, to burden the group means that the group is burdened by it. And in poetry: She is burdened by her buttocks The rump is not burdened by it, but it is burdened by the rump. Al-A’sha said: I was not immersed in the fierce war when its fuel was its stumps.

Some of the Kufian Arabists rejected what this speaker said, and the beginning of in after ma, and said that it is permissible with ma and min, and it is better with ma and min than with alladhi, because alladhi does not work on its relative clause, nor does its relative clause work on it, so that is why it is permissible, and the sentence became the pronoun of ma, since it does not work on ma, nor does ma work on it. He said: It is good with ma and min, because they can be interpreted as indefinite if you like, or as definite if you like, so you say: I hit a man so that he may stand up, and I hit a man because he is a good man, so min and ma are the interpretation of this, and with alladhi it is uglier, because it cannot be interpreted as indefinite. Another of them said about his statement, to burden the group: its burden on the group: that it weighs them down. The meaning said: Its keys are to burden the group: they are moved by its weight.

So if you insert the preposition ba you say it burdens them, as he said, Bring me molten copper that I may pour over it (al-Kahf 18:96). He said: The meaning is: Bring me molten copper that I may pour over it. So if you delete the preposition ba, you add an alif to the beginning of the verb. Similar to it is The childbirth pains came to her
r
(Maryam 19:23)

. Its meaning is: The childbirth pains brought her. He said: A man from the people of Arabic said: The group cannot bear its keys, so he changed the verb to keys, as the poet said: A lamp is a source of pride for the noble one, and the eye is adorned with it if it abandons it. It is the one that is adorned by the eye. He said: If he heard a trace of this, then it is a face, otherwise the man did not know the meaning. He said: And some Arabs recited to me: Even if the continuity is united and the distance between the north and the south is his shoulders Meaning: When the archer took the bow and drew wealth from it.

He said: We see that the Arabs say: Ma sadaka wa faraaka min-al-min, meaning: Ma sadaka wa faraaka min-al-min, except that they dropped the alif because it follows sa’ak, just as the Arabs said: I ate food so he congratulated me and he pleased me, meaning: if you singularize wa faraana and drop the alif from it because it follows something that does not have an alif. This other interpretation of His statement, that it would be too much for a band of men, is more correct than the other statements, for two reasons: First, that it is an interpretation that is in accordance with the apparent meaning of the revelation. Second, that the narrations we have mentioned from the people of interpretation came in a similar sense. And the statement of those who said that its meaning is: that a band of men would not be able to bear its keys, is only an explanation from them that it means: that a band of men could not carry its keys.

And if it is explained in this way, then there is no indication in it that what is meant by it is report of the abundance of His treasures, in the same way as if it is explained that its meaning is: that His keys would burden a band of men and make them incline, because a band of men can carry a few keys or a lot. Rather, the Exalted intended to report their abundance. And if what is meant by it is report of their abundance, then there is no doubt that what was said by those we have mentioned, that its meaning is: that a band of men could not carry its keys, is a statement that has no meaning. This is in addition to it being contrary to the interpretation of the early generations on that. And His saying, “
h
When his people said to him
h
Do not rejoice
. Indeed, God does not like the exultant.’” He says: When his people said, “Do not seek or be arrogant with exultation. Indeed, God does not like the wicked and the arrogant among His creation.”
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, Indeed, God does not like the exultant, meaning: the merry ones.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
Do not rejoice
. Indeed, God does not like the exultant,” he said: The extravagant, the wicked, the arrogant, who do not associate partners with God in what He has given them.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Jabir, who said:
m: I heard Mujahid say about this verse, Indeed, God does not like the exultant. He said: The arrogant, the haughty, the extravagant.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
Do not rejoice
. Indeed, God does not like the exultant,” he said: He means transgression.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, “
h
Do not rejoice
. Indeed, God does not like the exultant,” he said: The extravagant and wicked, who do not thank God for what He has given them.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, except that he said: the extravagant.

c: Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Mukhrami told us, he said: Shababah told me, he said: Warqa’ told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Do not rejoice
, for God does not love the exultant. He said: The arrogant and haughty.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
when his people said to him
h
Do not rejoice
: that is, do not be merry, for God does not love those who are merry: that is, God does not love those who are merry.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjajin told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Do not rejoice
, for God does not like the rejoicing. He said: The arrogant and haughty, who do not thank God for what He has given them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
When his people said to him
h
Do not rejoice
. Indeed, God does not like the exultant.’” He said: It is the joy of transgression.

x: God Almighty says, informing us of what Qarun's people said to him: Do not seek, O Qarun, against your people, with your abundant wealth, but seek the good things of the Hereafter from the wealth that God has given you, by working in it in obedience to God in this world. And His statement,
h
And do not neglect your portion of this world

, means: Do not abandon your portion and fortune in this world, lest you take your portion of the Hereafter in it, and work in it in a way that will save you from God's punishment tomorrow. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And do not neglect your portion of this world and do good as God has done good to you
, meaning: Do not neglect to work for God in this world.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And do not forget your portion of this world. He said: To work in it for your afterlife.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Qura bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah,
m: And do not forget your share of this world. He said: Some people place it in a bad place, and do not forget your share of this world, and work in it in obedience to God.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And do not forget your share of this world. He said: Working in obedience to Him.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Work in your worldly life for the sake of your afterlife.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And do not neglect your portion of this world
, he said: Working in it in obedience to God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Isa Al-Jarashi, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And do not forget your portion of this world. He said: To work in this world for the sake of your afterlife.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Working in obedience to God is his share of this world, for which he will be rewarded in the Hereafter.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And do not neglect your portion of this world
, he said: Do not forget to send forth from your worldly life for your afterlife, for you will only find in your afterlife what you sent forth in this world through what God has provided for you.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Do not neglect to seek your share of sustenance in it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And do not forget your share of this world. Al-Hasan said: What God has made lawful for you from it, for in it you will find sufficiency and contentment.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Hamid Al-Ma’mari told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And do not neglect your portion of this world
. He said: Seeking what is lawful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And do not forget your share of this world. He said: Give priority to what is best, and hold back what you get.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: What is permissible is in it. His saying,
h
And do good as God has been good to you

, means: And do good in this world by spending your money that God has given you, in His ways and paths, as God has been good to you, by making it abundant for you and expanding it for you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And do good as God has been good to you

, he said: Do good with what God has provided for you. And do not seek corruption on earth, he said: Do not seek what God has forbidden you of transgressing against your people. Indeed, God does not like corrupters, he said: God does not like those who seek transgression and sin.

x: God Almighty says: Qarun said to his people who had admonished him: I was given these treasures because of the superior knowledge I have, which God taught me, and He was pleased with me for that, and He favored me with this money over you, because He knew of my superiority over you. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: “He said:
h
It was only given to me because of knowledge I have
.” He said: Because of report I have. He said: Yunus told me, he said:

c: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
It was only given to me because of knowledge I have

, he said: If it were not for God’s pleasure with me and His knowledge of my virtue, He would not have given me this. And he recited, Does he not know that God destroyed before him generations who were stronger than him in strength and greater in accumulation?... the verse. It has been said that the meaning of his saying I have is: I see, as if he said: I was given it because of the superiority of my knowledge, as I see it. And His statement,
h
Did he not know that God had destroyed before him generations who were mightier than him in strength and greater in accumulation

? God, the Most High, says: Didn’t Qarun know, when he claimed that he had been given treasures because of superior knowledge he had that I knew from him, and thus deserved to be given what he had been given of treasures, that God had destroyed before him nations who were mightier than him in power and greater in accumulation of wealth? If God had given wealth to whomever He gave it, due to superiority and goodness in it, and due to His pleasure with them, He would not have destroyed those of the wealthy who had more wealth than him, because if God is pleased with someone, it is impossible for God to destroy him while He is pleased with him. Rather, He only destroys those with whom He is angry. And His saying,
h
And the criminals will not be asked about their sins
, it was said that the meaning of this is that they will enter Hell without being held to account.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us:
m: He said: Al-Hussein narrated to us: He said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Umar, on the authority of Qatada:
h
And the criminals will not be asked about their sins
. He said: They will enter Hell without being held to account. It was said: The meaning of this is that the angels will not be asked about them, because they know them by their appearance.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And the criminals will not be asked about their sins

, like His statement, The criminals will be known by their mark Ar-Rahman 55:41, blue-eyed with black faces, and the angels will not be asked about them, they have known them. And it was said that the meaning of this is: And the criminals will not be asked about the sins of those whom God destroyed from the past nations, among whom the criminals were destroyed.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b,
m: h
And the criminals will not be asked about their sins
, he said: About the sins of those who have passed away, for what they were destroyed. So the ha’ and the mim in His statement,
h
About their sins
, according to this interpretation, are for whom is mentioned in His statement,
h
Does he not know that God destroyed before him generations who were mightier than him in strength

? And according to the first interpretation, which was given by Mujahid and Qatadah, it is for the criminals, and it is more appropriate for it to be from the mention of the criminals, because God, the Exalted, will not be asked about the sins of a sinner other than the one who sinned, neither a believer nor a disbeliever. If that is the case, then it is known that there is no meaning to the criminals being specific, if the ha’ and the mim in His statement,
h
About their sins

, were for whom is mentioned in His statement, whom is mightier than him in strength, excluding the believers, meaning because neither a believer nor a disbeliever is asked about that, except those who have done it and acquired it. Surat al-Qasas 28:78 He said, "It has only been given to me because of knowledge I have." Does he not know that God had destroyed before him generations stronger than him in strength and greater in multitude?
h
And the criminals will not be asked about their sins

x: God Almighty says: So Korah came out to his people in his finery, which was, as mentioned, purple clothing.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Asim told us: Talha bin Amr told us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir:
m: He came out to his people in his finery. He said: In crimson. He said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said:

c: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
So he came out to his people in his finery
. He said: In red clothes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: He came out to his people in his finery. He said: On white mules, on which were purple saddles, and on which were saffron-colored garments.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
So he came out to his people in his finery
, he said: He was wearing two saffron-colored garments. Ibn Jurayj said: On a gray mule with purple on it, and three hundred slave girls on gray mules, wearing red clothes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father and Yahya bin Yaman told me, on the authority of Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He came out to his people in his finery. He said: In red and yellow clothes.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Samak,
m: that he heard Ibrahim Al-Nakhaʿi say about this verse,
h
So he came out to his people in his finery
, he said: in red clothes.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said: Ghundar told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: similarly.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ali al-Muqaddami told us: Ismail ibn Hakim told us:
m: We entered upon Malik ibn Dinar one evening, and he was mentioning Qarun. He said: And there was a man from his neighbors wearing saffron-colored clothes. Malik said: He came out to his people in his finery. He said: In clothes like this one’s clothes.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
So he came out to his people in his finery
. He told us that they came out on four thousand animals, and they and their animals were purple.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So he came out to his people in his finery

, he said: He went out with seventy thousand, wearing saffron, as my father used to tell us, Those who desired the life of this world said, ‘Oh, would that we had like that which was given to Korah!’ God Almighty says: Those among Korah’s people who desired the adornments of the life of this world said, Oh, would that we had been given like that which was given to Korah of its adornments! “Indeed, he is one of great fortune!” He says: Korah has a share of this world.

x: God the Almighty says: And those who were given knowledge of God said, when they saw Korah coming out before them in their finery, to those who said, Oh, would that we had like that which Korah has been given, "Woe to you! Fear God and obey Him." Indeed, the reward and recompense of God for those who believe in Him and His messengers, and do what His messengers brought of righteous deeds in the Hereafter is better than what Korah was given of his finery and wealth. And His statement, "
h
And none shall attain it except the patient
," means: and none shall attain it, meaning none shall be granted the opportunity to say this statement, which is His statement, "
h
The reward of God is better for him who believes and does righteousness

," and the ha and the alif are a metaphor for the word. And He said, "Except the patient," meaning by that: those who are patient and refrain from seeking the adornments of worldly life, and prefer the abundant reward of God for righteous deeds over the pleasures and desires of this world, so they strive in obeying God and rejecting this worldly life.

God Almighty says: So We caused the earth to swallow up Korah and the people of his house. It was also said: and his house, because it was mentioned that when Moses ordered the earth to take him, he ordered it to take him, and took those who were with him from among his companions in his house, and they were a group sitting with him, and they were in the same state of hypocrisy and support in harming Moses.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Al-A’mash informed us, on the authority of Al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When the zakat was revealed, Qarun came to Moses and made a deal with him for one dinar for every thousand dinars, and one thing for every thousand things, or he said: and every thousand sheep, one sheep. Al-Tabari is not sure. He said: Then he went to his house and counted it and found it to be a lot. So he gathered the Children of Israel and said: O Children of Israel, Moses commanded you to do everything and you obeyed him, and now he wants to take from your wealth. They said: You are our leader and you are our master, so order us to do whatever you wish. He said: I order you to bring the prostitute so-and-so and give her a reward, so she may accuse him of adultery. So they called her and he gave her a reward to accuse him of adultery. Then he came to Moses and said: The Children of Israel have gathered together so that you may command them and forbid them. So he went out to them while they were in a wide open land and said: O Children of Israel, whoever steals, we will cut off his hand. Whoever slanders, we will flog him. Whoever commits adultery and does not have a wife, we will flog him a hundred times. Whoever commits adultery and has a wife, we will flog him until he dies, or we will stone him until he dies. At-Tabari is not sure. Korah said to him: What if it was you? He said: What if it was me. He said: The Children of Israel claim that you committed adultery with so-and-so. He said: Call her, and if she says so, then it is as she said. So when she came, Moses said to her: O so-and-so. She said: Yes, I am at your service. He said: Did I do to you what these people say? She said: No, and they lied. Rather, they made a promise to me that I would throw myself at you. So he jumped up and prostrated while he was among them. Then God revealed to him: Command the earth as you wish. He said: O earth, take them. So it took them to their feet. Then he said: O earth, take them. So it took them to their knees. Then he said: O earth, take them. So it took them to their rights. Then he said: O earth, take them. So it took them to their necks. He said: So they began to say: O Moses, O Moses, and they begged him. He said: O earth, take them. So it closed over them. Then God revealed to him: O Moses, My servants say to you: O Moses, O Moses, yet you do not have mercy on them? If they had called upon Me, they would have found Me near and responsive. He said: That is the saying of God: So he came out to his people in his finery. His finery was that he came out on blond beasts with red saddles, wearing garments dyed with behroman. “Those who desired the life of this world said: ‘Oh, would that we had like that which was given to Korah!’” ... to His saying: Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed. “O Muhammad,” “That is the home of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.”

c: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya bin Isa narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Minhal, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: When God commanded Moses to pay the zakat, he said: They accused him of adultery, and he was alarmed by that, so they sent to a woman to whom they had given her judgment, on the condition that she accuse him herself. When she came, he was upset with her, and asked her: By He who parted the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Moses, should she tell the truth? She said: Since you have made me swear, I am more certain that you are innocent and that you are the Messenger of God. So he fell down in prostration, weeping, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: What makes you weep? We have given you power over the earth, so command it as you wish. He said: Take them. So it took them to whatever God willed. They said: O Moses, O Moses. He said: Take them. So it took them to whatever God willed. They said: O Moses, O Moses. So He caused the earth to swallow them up. He said: After that, the Children of Israel were afflicted with severe hardship and famine, so they came to Moses and said: Call upon your Lord for us. He said: So he called upon them, and God revealed to him: O Moses, are you speaking to me about a people whose sins have darkened the relationship between me and them? They called upon you and you did not answer them, but if they had called upon me, I would have answered them. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. He said: The earth was told, Take them, so it took them up to their heels. Then it was told, Take them, so it took them up to their knees. Then it was told, Take them, so it took them up to their loins. Then it was told, Take them, so it took them up to their necks. Surat al-Qasas 28:81 So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. And there was for him no company to aid him other than God, nor was he of those who defend themselves. Then it was told, Take them, so it swallowed them up. That is what He said, So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Ali bin Hashim bin Al-Barid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding the statement of God, Indeed, Korah was from the people of Moses, he said: He was his cousin, and Moses used to judge in a region of the Children of Israel, and Korah used to be in a region. He said: So he called a prostitute who was among the Children of Israel and gave her a reward to throw herself at Moses, but she left him. On the day when the Children of Israel would gather to Moses, Korah would come to him and say: O Moses, what is the punishment for one who steals? He said: That his hand be cut off. He said: And if it was you? He said: Yes. He said: What is the punishment for one who commits adultery? He said: That he be stoned. He said: And if it was you? He said: Yes. He said: Then you did it. He said: Woe to you, because of whom? He said: Because of so-and-so. Moses called her and said: I ask you by He who sent down the Torah, is Korah telling the truth? She said: O God, if you ask me, then I firmly believe that you are innocent, that you are the Messenger of God, and that the enemy of God, Qarun, has made a pledge to me to throw myself at you. Moses jumped up and fell prostrate before him, and God revealed to him: Raise your head, for you have commanded the earth to obey you. Moses said: O earth, take them. So it took them until they reached the hollows. He said: O Moses. He said: Take them. So it took them until they reached the chests. He said: O Moses. He said: Take them. He said: So they left. He said: Then God revealed to him: O Moses, he sought your help but you did not help him. If he had sought My help, I would have answered him and helped him.

c: Bishr bin Hilal al-Sawaaf narrated to us, saying: Ja’far bin Sulayman al-Dab’i narrated to us, saying: Ali bin Zayd bin Jud’an narrated to us, saying:
m: Abdullah bin al-Harith left the house and entered the chamber. When he came out of it, he sat down and leaned on it, and we sat beside him. Then Solomon bin Dawud mentioned, And he said, ‘O eminent ones, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?’ (al-Naml 27:28)… until His saying, Indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous. (al-Naml 27:40). Then he stopped mentioning Solomon, saying, Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he transgressed against them. He had been given treasures that God mentioned in His Book, Its keys would not be a burden to a company of strong men. “He said, ‘I have only been given it because of knowledge I have.’” He said, “And he became an enemy of Moses, and he was harmful to him, but Moses would pardon him and forgive him, because of the kinship, until he built a house, and made the door of his house of gold, and he put gold plates on its walls. The leaders of the Children of Israel would come to him morning and evening, and he would feed them.” Food, and they would talk to him and make him laugh, but his misery and affliction did not leave him, until he sent for a woman from the Children of Israel who was known for her immorality, and was famous for cursing. He sent for her and she came to him, and he said to her: Would you like me to finance you and give you money, and mix you with my women, on the condition that you come to me while the leaders of the Children of Israel are with me, and you say: O Qarun, will you not forbid Moses from me? She said: Yes. So when Qarun sat down and the leaders of the Children of Israel came, he sent for her, and she came and stood before him, and God changed her heart and caused her to repent, so she said to herself: For me to repent today is better than harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and accusing the enemy of God of lying to him. She said: Korah said to me: Would you like me to give you money and give you gifts, and mix you with my women, on the condition that you come to me while the leaders of the Children of Israel are with me, and you say: O Korah, will you not forbid Moses from me? I did not find a better repentance than not to harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to lie to the enemy of God. When I said these words, Korah fell into his hands, and he lowered his head, and the leaders were silent, and he knew that he had fallen into destruction, and her words spread among the people until they reached Moses. When they reached Moses, his anger intensified, so he performed ablution with water, prayed, and wept, and said: O Lord, your enemy is harmful to me, he wants to disgrace me and shame me. O Lord, give me power over him. So God revealed to him: Command the earth as you wish and it will obey you. So Moses came to Korah, and when he entered upon him, he recognized the evil in Moses’ face towards him, so he said: O Moses, have mercy on me. He said: O earth, take them. His house shook and sank with Korah and his companions up to their ankles, and he kept saying: O Moses, So I took them to their knees, and he was supplicating to Moses: O Moses, have mercy on me. He said: O earth, take them. He said: So his house shook and sank, and the earth swallowed Korah and his companions up to their couches, and he was supplicating to Moses: O Moses, have mercy on me. He said: O earth, take them. So the earth swallowed him up, along with his house and his companions. He said: And it was said to Moses, peace be upon him: O Moses, how rude you are. By My Glory, if he called to Me, I would answer him.

c: Bishr bin Hilal told me: Jaafar bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Jawni, who said:
m: It reached me that it was said to Moses: I will never worship the earth for anyone after you.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and Abd al-Hamid al-Hammani told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Aghar ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifah ibn Husayn.
m: Abd al-Hamid said, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Mahdi did not mention Abu Nasr, So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. He said: The seventh earth.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: We have been informed that he is swallowed up by a hundred cubits every day, and he will not reach the bottom of the earth until the Day of Resurrection, so he will continue to sink into it until the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Zaid bin Hibban told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Sulayman, who said:
m: I heard Malik bin Dinar say: It has reached me that Qarun is swallowed up by the earth a hundred cubits every day.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. He told us that he would be swallowed up by the earth a foot every day, and that he would sink into it, not reaching its bottom until the Day of Resurrection. And His statement, And he had no company to aid him other than God, means that he had no army to return to, nor any company to aid him when His wrath descended upon him. Rather, they disavowed him. And he was not among those who defend themselves, means that he was not among those who defend themselves against God when He brought down His wrath upon him, and thus he was protected from it by his strength. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: So he had no company to help him, meaning no army to help him, and he had no protection with which to protect himself from God. We have previously explained the meaning of the word group and that it is a group of people. Its origin is the group to which a man turns when he needs them, to help him against the enemy. Then the Arabs used this term for every group that helps and supports a man. From this comes the saying of Khafaf: I have never seen anyone like them, alive and pure. I found you between a camel and a stone. I am more patient than the vicissitudes of life and more patient than them.

x: God Almighty says: And those who wished for his place in this world yesterday, and his wealth and his abundance of money, and what was spread out for him of it yesterday, meaning before what befell him of God’s wrath and punishment befell him, they say: And it is as if God...
There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of and it is as if God as for Qatada, two opinions were narrated from him regarding this: One of them: What:

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthma told us: Saeed ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said
m: regarding his statement,
h
And it is as if he
: Did you not see that he...

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: And it is as if: Do you not see that he...

c: Ismail bin Al-Mutawakkil Al-Ashja’i told me, he said: Muhammad bin Katheer told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And it is as if he
he said: Did you not see that he... The other saying: What:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And it is as if God expands provision, he said: Did he not know that God and it is as if: Did he not know that He… This interpretation that we mentioned from Qatada was also interpreted by some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs, and he cited as evidence for the correctness of his interpretation the words of the poet: She asked me for divorce if she saw me. I have no money. You have done something reprehensible. And whoever has a lineage loves a child, and whoever is poor lives a life of hardship.

x: Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Wa-yaka'an in the speech of the Arabs means confirmation, like the man saying: Do you not see the creation of God and His benevolence? He mentioned that he was told by someone who heard a Bedouin woman saying to her husband: Where is our son? So he said: Wa-yaka'anhu is behind the house, meaning: Do you not see him behind the house? He said: Some grammarians may take it as two words, meaning: Woe to him, as if he meant woe to you, so he deleted the lam, so an is made open with an implied verb, as if he said: Woe to you, know that he is behind the house, so he implied know. We did not find the Arabs making an implied, nor knowledge and the like in an, because it is invalid if it is between two words, or at the end of a word, so when it is implied it is treated as a later word. Do you not see that it is not permissible at the beginning to say: O this one, that you are standing, and O this one that you stood, meaning: I knew, or I know, or I thought, or I think.

As for deleting the lam from your saying: Woe to you until it becomes: Woe to you, the Arabs may say it, because of its frequency in speech. Antara said: The saying of the knights, Woe to Antar, has healed my soul and cured its illness. He said: Others said: The meaning of his saying and it is as if is and separate from it is as if, like when you say to a man: Woe! Don’t you see what is before you? So he said: Woe! then he started again, as if God expands provision, and it is an expression of amazement, and as if has the meaning of suspicion and knowledge, so this is a correct interpretation. He said: The Arabs did not write it separately, and if it were like this, they would have written it separately. It is also possible that there was a lot of talk about it, so it was connected to something that is not from it.
