Another of them said: Wa is an alert, and ka’an is another letter other than it, meaning: perhaps the matter is thus, and I think the matter is thus, because ka’an is like I think, “I think,” and I know.

The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying we mentioned on the authority of Qatada, that its meaning is: Did you not see, did you not know? This is based on the evidence we mentioned in it from the words of the poet and the narration from the Arabs, and that َويكاأin the script of the Mushaf is one letter. When this is directed to something other than the interpretation we mentioned on the authority of Qatada, then it becomes two letters. This is because if it is directed to the saying of someone who interprets it to mean: Woe to you, I know that God, thenويكاmust be separated from َأ, and this is contrary to the script of all the Mushafs, in addition to its corruption in Arabic, for what we mentioned. If it is directed to the saying of someone who says:ويكاin the meaning of alerting, then he starts the speech again with َكا, then it is based on the saying of someone who saysويكاin the meaning of َكا, and this is also contrary to the script of all the Mushafs.

Surat al-Qasas 28:82 And those who had wished for his place the day before began to say, "It is as if God extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. Had it not been that God has bestowed favor upon us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up."
h
And it is as if the disbelievers will not succeed

. If that was a single letter, then the correct interpretation is what Qatada said. Since that is the correct interpretation, then the statement is: And those who wished for the place of Qarun and his position in this world yesterday, said when they witnessed the punishment that God had brought upon him: Have you not seen, O man, that God expands provision for whomever He wills of His servants, and He makes it abundant for him, not because of the superiority of his status with Him, nor because of His honor towards him, just as He expanded that for Qarun, not because of His honor or honor towards him.

And He restricts means: And He restricts that for whomever He wills of His creation, and He restricts it for him, not because of his humiliation, nor because of His displeasure with his work. His saying, Had it not been that God had been gracious to us, means: Had He not been gracious to us and diverted from us what we had wished for yesterday, the earth would have swallowed us up. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions, except Shaiba, read it as lakhasfa bena with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the seen.

m: It was reported from Shaiba and Al-Hasan as lakhasfa bena with a fatha on the kha and the seen, meaning: God caused the earth to swallow us up. And His saying,
h
And it is as if the disbelievers will not succeed
, means: Did you not know that the disbelievers will not succeed, and that their requests will succeed?

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.
The majority of the reciters of the regions, except Shaiba, read it as lakhasfa bena with a damma on the kha and a kasra on the seen.

x: God Almighty says: That is the home of the Hereafter. We assign its pleasures to those who do not desire arrogance or tyranny over the truth on earth, nor corruption: meaning: nor oppression of people unjustly, nor committing sins against God therein. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Abi Ziyad, who said:
m: I heard Ikrimah say, They do not desire to be arrogant or to cause corruption on earth. He said: Arrogance means tyranny.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin,
m: “That is the home of the Hereafter. We assign it to those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth or corruption.” He said: Exaltation means arrogance in the truth, and corruption means taking what is not right.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin:
m: For those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth he said: arrogance upon the earth without right nor corruption taking money without right. He said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
h
For those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth
, he said: transgression.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement,
h
For those who do not desire exaltation upon the earth
, he said: arrogance and tyranny, nor corruption, he said: committing sins.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ash’ath al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Salman al-A’raj, on the authority of Ali,
m: may God be pleased with him, who said: A man may be pleased with the fact that the strap of his sandal is better than the strap of his companion, so it is included in the words of God Almighty: “That is the home of the Hereafter which We assign to those who do not desire exaltedness upon the earth or corruption. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.” And His statement,
h
And the best outcome is for the righteous

, God Almighty says: And Paradise is for the righteous, and they are those who avoid the sins of God and perform His obligations. And in a similar manner to what we said about the meaning of the consequence, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the best outcome is for the righteous
, meaning Paradise is for the righteous.

x: God Almighty says: Whoever comes to God on the Day of Resurrection with sincere monotheism, then he will have good, and that good is Paradise and eternal bliss. And whoever comes with evil, which is associating partners with God.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it

: meaning he will have a good portion of it. The good deed is sincerity, and the bad deed is polytheism. We have explained this based on the differences of those who differ, and we have shown the correct statement about it. His statement, Those who do evil deeds will not be recompensed, means: Those who do evil deeds will not be rewarded for their evil deeds, except for what they used to do, meaning: except for the recompense for what they used to do.

x: God Almighty says: He who sent down to you, O Muhammad, the Qur’an.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an, he said: He who gave you the Qur’an.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an, he said: He who gave it to you. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement, To return you to a place of return.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: To return you to Paradise.
Who said that?

c: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shaheed told me: Atab bin Bishr told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: To your place of return in Paradise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: To Paradise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told me, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Hibban,
m: who heard Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri:
h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: His place of return is Paradise.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely return you to a place of return, he said: To Paradise, so that He may ask you about the Qur’an.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said:
m: Paradise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih:
m: h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: To Paradise.

c: Yahya bin Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik, who said:
m: He will return you to Paradise, then he will ask you about the Qur’an.

c: Abu Kurayb told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah and Mujahid, who said:
m: To Paradise.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: Ata’, Mujahid, Abu Qaz’ah, and Al-Hasan, they said: On the Day of Resurrection. He said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:

c: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Al-Zuhri, they said:
m: His return is on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
He will return you to a place of return
, he said: He will bring you on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Awn told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement,
h
He will return you to a place of return
, he said: Your place of return is in the Hereafter.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement,
h
He will return you to a place of return
, he said: Al-Hasan used to say: Yes, by God, he has a place of return in which God will resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection and admit him into Paradise.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: to bring you back to death.
Who said that?

c: Ishaq bin Wahb Al-Wasiti told me, he said: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Zubayri told us, he said: Sufyan bin Saeed Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
He will return you to a place of return

, he said: death. Surat al-Qasas 28:85 Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely bring you back to a place of return. Say, “My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance and who is in manifest error.”

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Until death. He said: My father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: To death.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of someone
m: who heard Ibn Abbas, who said: Until death.

c: Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Until death.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding his statement:
h
He will return you to a place of return
, he said: Death.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Abu Tamila told us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Adi bin Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: To death, or to Mecca.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: to return you to the place from which you left, which is Mecca.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Asfari, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: To Mecca.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: He says: He will return you to Mecca, just as He expelled you from it.

c: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Yunus bin Abi Ishaq told us, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: He was born in Mecca.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us on the authority of Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq:
m: I heard Mujahid say:
h
He will return you to a place of return
. He said: To your birthplace in Mecca.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us:
m: Yunus bin Amr, who is the son of Abi Ishaq, told us on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will surely bring you back to a place of return, he said: To your birthplace in Mecca.

c: Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i told me: My father told us, on the authority of al-Fudayl ibn Marzuq, on the authority of Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj,
m: regarding his statement: Indeed, He who has enjoined upon you the Qur’an will return you to a place of return, he said: To his birthplace in Mecca.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: To your birth in Mecca. The correct statement in this regard, in my opinion, is the statement of those who said: To bring you back to your custom from death, or To your custom where you were born. This is because the resurrection in this case is the passive participle of habit, not of return. Unless the interpretation of his statement To bring you back is directed to your destination, then his statement to a return is directed to the meaning of return, and its interpretation is: He who imposed the Qur’an upon you is for your destination until you return to Mecca, opened for you.

x: We have understood these aspects that were described in this regard, so what is the interpretation of those who interpret it as meaning: He will return you to Paradise?
The interpretation of this should be the same in this other way, which is He will return you to Paradise.
Was he expelled from Paradise, and it was said to him: We will return you to it?

There are two aspects to this: One of them is that if his father Adam (peace be upon them) was expelled from it, then it is as if his children, by God’s expulsion of him from it, were expelled from it. So whoever enters it is as if he will be returned to it after his exit.

The second is that it is said: He (peace be upon him) entered it on the night of his Ascension, as it was narrated from him that he said: “I entered Paradise and saw a palace in it, so I said: ‘Whose is this?’ They said: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab,’” and similar reports were narrated from him about that. Then he was returned to Earth, and it was said to him: He who enjoined the Qur’an upon you will return you to the place from which you were expelled from Paradise, until you return to it. This is, God willing, the statement of the one who said that. And His statement: Say, ‘My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance and who is in clear error.’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: My Lord is most knowing of who has brought guidance, whoever follows it will be saved, and who among us and you is deviating from the right path.
And His statement, clear, means that He makes clear to the thinking, understanding person, if he ponders and contemplates it, that it is misguidance and deviance from the right path.

God Almighty says: And you did not expect, O Muhammad, that this Qur’an would be sent down to you, so that you would learn the report and information about those who came before you and what will come after you, of what has not happened yet, of what you have not witnessed and will not witness, and then recite it to your people from Quraysh, except that your Lord had mercy on you and sent it down to you. So His statement: except as a mercy from your Lord is an interrupted exception. And His statement:
h
So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers

, meaning: So thank your Lord for the mercy He has bestowed upon you by sending down this Book to you, and do not be an aid to those who disbelieve in it. It has been said that this is from the deferred meaning of bringing forward, and that the meaning of the lam is: He who imposed the Qur’an upon you and sent it down to you, and you did not hope that it would be sent down to you, so that you would be a prophet before that, will return you to the place of return.

evidence.text: God Almighty says: And you did not expect, O Muhammad, that this Qur’an would be sent down to you, so that you would learn the report and information about those who came before you and what will come after you, of what has not happened yet, of what you have not witnessed and will not witness, and then recite it to your people from Quraysh, except that your Lord had mercy on you and sent it down to you.

x: God Almighty says: And do not let these polytheists turn you away from conveying the verses of God and His proofs after your Lord has revealed them to you, O Muhammad, with their saying, Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given? And call to your Lord and convey His message to whomever He sent you with it. And do not be among those who associate others with God. He says: And do not abandon calling to your Lord and conveying His message to the polytheists, lest you be among those who do the actions of the polytheists by disobeying your Lord and going against His command.

God Almighty says: O Muhammad, do not worship any other god besides Him, along with your God, to whom all things are entitled to worship. And His statement, There is no god but Him, means: There is no god worthy of worship except God, to whom all things perish
h
except His Face
. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of his statement:
h
Except His Face
Some of them said: It means: Everything will perish except Him.
Others said: The meaning of this is: except what is intended for His sake.

i: They cited as evidence for their interpretation of this the words of the poet:
x: I ask forgiveness of God for a sin that I cannot count.

To Him belongs the face and the action. His statement: His is the judgment, meaning: He is the judgment among His creation, and no one else has judgment over them with Him. And to Him you will be returned, meaning: And to Him you will be returned after your death, and He will judge between you with justice, rewarding your believers with their reward, and your disbelievers with what He promised them.

notes.en: This is how it appears in Ṣ, T1, T2, and T3; M reads: “continuously.” The wording is disordered and something is omitted. Al-Farrāʾ explains in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān 2/305 that “mā,” a particle used in conditional constructions, is joined with “ayy.” In ʿAbd Allāh’s reading it is: “Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there shall be no reproach against me.” He then discusses the point the author will quote from him below.
notes.ar: كذا في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3، وفى م: "على الدوام"، وفى العبارة اضطراب وسقط، وقال الفراء في معاني القرآن 2/ 305: فجعل "ما" وهى صلة من صلات الجزاء مع "أي" وهي في قراءة عبد الله: (أي الأجلين ما قضيت فلا عدوان على). ثم ذكر الكلام الآتي الذي سيذكره المصنف عنه بعدُ.

notes.ar: أخرجه ابن عساكر في تاريخ دمشق 66/ 333 من طريق ابن عيينة به، وأخرجه النسائي في الكبرى (11384) مِن طريق عمرو به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 133، 134 إلى سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وأبى داود في القدر وابن المنذر وابن مردويه.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 530; through him, Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s Tafsīr 9/3994. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/134 to al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.

notes.en: M reads: “al-aṣamm.” Aṣāhu means “he turned it around and tried it on him.” Al-Nihāyah 4/276.
notes.ar: في م: "الأصم". وألاصه: أداره عليها، ورواده عليها. النهاية 4/ 276.

notes.en: AḌaḥḍāḥ originally means shallow water spread over the ground, reaching about the ankles; here it is used metaphorically for fire. Al-Nihāyah 3/75.
notes.ar: الضحضاح في الأصل: ما رَقَّ من الماء على وجه الأرضِ ما يبلغ الكعبين. فاستعاره للنار. النهاية 3/ 75.

notes.en: Hannād transmitted a similar report in al-Zuhd (no. 306) through ʿAṭāʾ.
notes.ar: أخرجه هناد في الزهد (306) من طريق عطاء به نحوه.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 530; through him, Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s Tafsīr 9/2995. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/134 to al-Firyābī, Ibn Abī Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 530، ومن طريقه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 2995، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 134 إلى الفريابي وابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Waṭṭaʾahu means “he prepared or made it ready for him.” Tāj al-ʿarūs, root w-ṭ-ʾ.
notes.ar: وطَّأه: هَيَّأه. تاج العروس (وط أ).

notes.en: Al-Nasāʾī transmitted it in al-Kubrā (no. 11385) through Ḥajjāj, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb reported from Ibn ʿAbbās—though he had not heard it directly from him—that al-Ḥārith ibn Nawfal was the one who said … up to God’s words “from our land.” Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/134 to Ibn al-Mundhir. Al-Qurṭubī cited a similar version in his Tafsīr 13/300.
notes.ar:
أخرجه النسائي في الكبرى (11385) من طريق حجاج عن ابن جريج عن ابن أبي مليكة قال: قال عمرو بِن شعيب عن ابن عباس، ولم يسمعه منه، أن الحارث بن نوفل الذي قال 
…. إلى قوله تعالى: {مِنْ أَرْضِنَا}، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 134 إلى ابن المنذر، وذكره القرطبي في تفسيره 13/ 300 بنحوه.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr 9/2995 from Muḥammad ibn Saʿd.
notes.ar: أخرجه أبى حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 2995 عن محمد بن سعد به.

notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 92 - ومن طريقه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 2996 - عن معمر به، وزاد في آخره: أو سلب.

notes.en: Ashar means exuberance and insolence; it is also said to mean extreme insolence, or joy expressed through arrogance and ingratitude for blessings. See Tāj al-ʿarūs, root ʾ-sh-r.
notes.ar: الأشر: المَرَح والبَطَر. وقيل: أشدُّ البطَر. وقيل: الأشر: الفرح بطَرًا وكُفرًا بالنِّعْمة. ينظر تاج العروس (أ ش ر).

notes.en: See the discussion above, 2/579–580.
notes.ar: ينظر ما تقدم في 2/ 579، 580.

notes.en: M reads: “ashar.”
notes.ar: في م: "أشر".

notes.ar: في م: "ظلم".

notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 299، 2999 من طريق يزيد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 5/ 135 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.ar: أخرجه الواحدى في أسباب النزول ص 255 من طريق شعبة به بنحوه وسيأتي ص 295.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “al-Thaʿlabī”; M: “al-Taghlibī.” The adopted form is from his biographical sources. See Tahdhīb al-Kamāl 4/28.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "الثعلبي"، وفى م: "التغلبى". والمثبت من مصادر ترجمته. ينظر تهذيب الكمال 4/ 28.

notes.en: Al-Wāḥidī transmitted it in Asbāb al-nuzūl, p. 255, through Badal ibn al-Muḥabbar.
notes.ar: أخرجه الواحدى فى أسباب النزول ص 255 من طريق بدل بن المحبر به

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 2/92 from Maʿmar. Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr 9/3000 through Saʿīd ibn Bashīr, from Qatādah. He also transmitted an extended version there through Shaybān, from the grammarian Qatādah, with the wording: “they are the jinn.” Al-Suyūṭī cites this wording at length in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/135, attributing it to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق فى تفسيره 2/ 92 عن معمر به، وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 9/ 3000 من طريق سعيد بن بشير، عن قتادة. وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 9/ 3000 مطولا من طريق شيبان، عن قتادة النحوى بلفظ: هم الجن. وبهذا اللفظ ذكره السيوطى مطولا في الدر المنثور 5/ 135، وعزاه إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 531; through him, Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s Tafsīr 9/3000. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/135 to al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهدٍ ص 531، ومن طريقه ابن أبي حاتم فى تفسيره 9/ 3000، وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 5/ 135 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Omitted in M and T1.
notes.ar: سقط من: م، ت 1.

notes.en: Tamattut derives from matt. Matt means seeking connection and approach through kinship, a sacred bond, or something else. See Tāj al-ʿarūs, root m-t-t.
notes.ar: التَّماتُّ من المتّ، والمَتُّ: التَّوسُّل والتَّوَصُّل بِقَرابةٍ أو حُرمةٍ أو غير ذلك. ينظر تاج العروس (م ت ت).

notes.en: Mujāhid’s Tafsīr, p. 531; through him, Ibn Abī Ḥātim’s Tafsīr 9/3000. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/135 to al-Firyābī, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir; these sources cite it only up to the words “through kinship.”
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهدٍ ص 531، ومن طريقه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 3000. وعزاه السيوطى في الدر المنثور 5/ 135 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر، وفى هذه المصادر إلى قوله: بالأنساب.

notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 3001، 3002 عن محمد بن سعد به.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “with things.” The reading in M is correct and agrees with the context.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "بالأشياء". والمثبت من م هو الصواب الموافق للسياق.

notes.en: Commentary on his Dīwān, p. 91. There it reads “Suhayya” instead of “Sumayyah,” and “that this one was” instead of “this one was.”
notes.ar: شرح ديوانه ص 91. وعنده:"سُهَيَّة" مكان "سمية"، و "أن ذا" مكان "كان ذا".

notes.en: By the particle of description here, he means min (“from”) in the verse’s phrase minki (“from you”).
notes.ar: يعني بحرف الصفة هنا: "مِنْ" فى قوله في البيت: "مِنْكِ".

notes.en: Commentary on his Dīwān, pp. 461–462. The second verse also appears in Lisān al-ʿArab, root s-l-f, with the author’s wording.
notes.ar: شرح ديوانه ص 461، 462. والبيت الثاني مذكور في اللسان (س ل ف). كرواية المصنف.

notes.en: Kalifa bi-l-shayʾ means “he became attached to it”; one may say kalif or mukallaf. Kalifa bihā ashadda al-kalaf means “he loved her intensely.” See Lisān al-ʿArab, root k-l-f.
notes.ar: كَلِف بالشيء فهو كلِف ومُكلَّف: لَهِج به. وكلِف بها أشدَّ الكَلَف. أي: أحبَّها. ينظر اللسان (ك ل ف).

notes.en: A muslif woman is middle-aged. It is also said that she has reached about forty-five; this description is specifically used of women. Lisān al-ʿArab, root s-l-f.
notes.ar: المسلف من النساء: النَّصَف. وقيل: هى التى بلغت خمسا وأربعين ونحوها، وهو وَصْف خُصَّ به الإناث. اللسان (س ل ف).

notes.en: M reads: “it is hidden”; T2: “it is permissible.” Akhāla al-shayʾ means “the thing seemed ambiguous.” One says, “This matter is not obscure to anyone,” meaning it is not confusing. Lisān al-ʿArab, root kh-y-l.
notes.ar: في م: "يخفى"، وفى ت 2: "يحل". وأخال الشيءُ: اشْتَبه. يقال: هذا الأمر لا يُخِيل على أحدٍ. أى لا يُشكل. اللسان (خ ى ل).

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr wrote in his Tafsīr 6/261 that, according to the stronger of two views, “they have no choice” is a negation, as in: “It is not for a believing man or woman, once God and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have a choice in it.” See al-Qurṭubī’s Tafsīr 13/305–306.
notes.ar: قال ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 261: وقوله: {مَا كَانَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ} نفى على أصح القولين، كقوله تعالى: {وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤْمِنٍ وَلَا مُؤْمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَمْرًا أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُمُ الْخِيَرَةُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ}. وينظر تفسير القرطبي 13/ 305، 306.

notes.en: M reads: “clearer.”
notes.ar: في م: "أوضح".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “the preceding.”
notes.ar: فى ص، ت 1، ت 2: "السابق".

notes.en: Omitted in M. The lexicons give al-ṭiyarah and al-ṭīrah; they also give al-ṭayr as the noun of taṭayyur. God knows best. See Lisān al-ʿArab and Tāj al-ʿarūs, root ṭ-y-r.
notes.ar: سقط من: م. والذى فى المعاجم "الطِّيَرَة والطِّيرة". وفيها أيضًا "الطَّيْر"وهو الاسم من "التطير". فالله أعلم. ينظر اللسان والتاج (ط ى ر).

notes.en: He is Abū ʿUbaydah, in Majāz al-Qurʾān 2/109, which reads: “about those.”
notes.ar: هو أبو عبيدة فى مجاز القرآن 2/ 109، وفيه: عن الذين.

notes.ar: فى م: "فإن". والمثبت من بقية النسخ موافق لنسخ التاريخ، وإن غيرها محقق التاريخ.

notes.en: M reads: “ʿAwmar.”
notes.ar: فى م: "عومر".

notes.en: The author transmitted it in his History 1/443. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/136 to Ibn al-Mundhir. The author’s History adds: “Thus al-Qāsim said; it is actually ʿUmram.”
notes.ar: أخرجه المصنف فى تاريخه 1/ 443، وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 5/ 136 إلى ابن المنذر، وزاد المصنف فى التاريخ: هكذا قال القاسم، وإنما هو عمرم.

notes.en: The author’s History reads: “Shimʿīt.” The adopted reading agrees with one copy of the History.
notes.ar: فى تاريخ المصنف: "شميت"، والمثبت موافق لإحدى نسخ التاريخ.

notes.ar: أخرجه البخارى (4773)، والنسائي (11386)، والبيهقى فى الدلائل 2/ 520، 521 من طريق يعلى به. وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 5/ 140 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Ibn Kathīr cited it in his Tafsīr 6/270 from al-ʿAwfī. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/140 to Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: ذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 6/ 270 عن العوفى به. وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 5/ 140 إلى ابن مردويه.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it in his Tafsīr 9/3026, and al-Bayhaqī in al-Dalāʾil 2/521, through Yūnus. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 5/140 to al-Firyābī and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره 9/ 3026، والبيهقى فى الدلائل 2/ 521 من طريق يونس به. وعزاه السيوطى فى الدر المنثور 5/ 140 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: M reads: “in Mecca.”
notes.ar: في م: "بمكة".

notes.en: Aḥmad transmitted it 14/178 (no. 8471); al-Bukhārī (nos. 3242, 3680, 5227, 7023, 7025), Muslim (no. 2395), and others transmitted it from Abū Hurayrah. Aḥmad 19/103 and 20/214, 296 (nos. 12046, 12834, 12983), al-Nasāʾī (no. 8127), and others transmitted it from Anas. Related reports are also transmitted from Jābir, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, and Buraydah al-Aslamī.
notes.ar: أخرجه أحمد 14/ 178 (8471)، والبخاري (3242، 3680، 5227، 7023، 7025) ومسلم (2395) وغيرهم من حديث أبي هريرة. وأخرجه أحمد 19/ 103، 20/ 214، 296 (12046، 12834، 12983)، والنسائي (8127) وغيرهما من حديث أنس. وفى الباب عن جابر ومعاذ بن جبل وبريدة الأسلمى.

notes.en: Ṣ and T2 add after it: “his people.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، ت 2: "قومه".

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, and T2 read: “and not.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2: "ولا".

notes.en: T1 and T2 read: “with you.”
notes.ar: فى ت 1، ت 2: "بك".

notes.en: T2 reads: “and not.”
notes.ar: في ت 2: "ولا".

notes.en: T2 reads: “I sent you.”
notes.ar: في ت 2: "أرسلتك".

notes.en: T1 adds after it: “except His face.”
notes.ar: بعده في ت 1: "إلا وجهه".

notes.en: Al-Farrāʾ’s Maʿānī al-Qurʾān 2/314; cited above, 1/170.
notes.ar: معانى القرآن للفراء 2/ 314، وتقدم فى 1/ 170.
